claims.statement: In Norse mythology Skinfaxi and Hrímfaxi are the horses of Dagr (day) and Nótt (night); the names mean 'shining mane' and 'frost mane', and froth from Hrímfaxi's bit is believed to fall to earth as dew.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Skinfaxi dan Hrímfaxi adalah kuda Dagr (siang) dan Nótt (malam); namanya berarti "surai bersinar" dan "surai berembun beku", dan buih dari kekang Hrímfaxi diyakini jatuh ke bumi menjadi embun.
claims.quote: In Norse mythology, Skinfaxi (Old Norse: [ˈskinˌfɑkse] ) and Hrímfaxi [ˈhriːmˌfɑkse] are the horses of Dagr (day) and Nótt (night). The names Skinfaxi and Hrímfaxi mean "shining mane" and "frost mane", respectively. ... "Froth" is believed to fall from Hrímfaxi's bit to the earth and become dew.

claims.statement: In the Danish account Hrymfaxe or Rimfaxe is the horse harnessed to the moon's chariot, drawing the moon across the night sky, its bit's foam falling as dew.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik versi Denmark, Hrymfaxe atau Rimfaxe adalah kuda yang ditambatkan pada kereta bulan, menarik bulan melintasi langit di malam hari, dan buih dari kekangnya jatuh sebagai embun.
claims.quote: Hrymfaxe eller Rimfaxe er i nordisk mytologi hesten, der er forspændt månevognen. Den trækker månen over himlen om natten. Skummet fra hestens bidsel falder som dug.

claims.statement: Rimfakse (Old Norse Hrímfaxi, 'rime in the mane') is the horse Night rides across the sky every night; morning dew drips from its bit, and Odin names it in the Vafþrúðnismál of the Elder Edda.
claims.statement_id: Rimfakse (Nordik Kuno Hrímfaxi, "embun beku di surai") adalah kuda yang ditunggangi Natt melintasi langit setiap malam; embun pagi menetes dari kekangnya, dan ia disebut Odin dalam Vafþrúðnismál di Edda Puisi.
claims.quote: Rimfakse (Norrønt:Hrímfaxi, rim i manen) er i norrøn mytologi den hesten Natt rir på over himmelen hver natt. Morgenduggen kom dryppende fra Rimfakses bissel. Rimfakse nevnes i Den eldre Edda, der Odin sier følgende i Vavtrudnesmål:

claims.statement: Oehlenschläger's poem Guldhornene mentions the sky horses, and the arms of Faxe Municipality show a stylised Hrymfaxe or Skinfaxe as a pun on the town's name.
claims.statement_id: Puisi Oehlenschläger Guldhornene menyebut kuda-kuda langit, dan lambang kotamadya Faxe menampilkan gambar bergaya Hrymfaxe atau Skinfaxe sebagai permainan kata nama kota itu.
claims.quote: Oehlenschlägers digt Guldhornene omtaler himmelhestene: ... Faxes kommunevåben forestiller en stilliseret tegning af Hrymfaxe hhv. Skinfaxe og repræsenterer et ordspil på byens/kommunens navn.

claims.statement: The Vafþrúðnismál stanza: 'Rimfakse is the horse that draws night over the noble gods; drops of foam he lets fall each morning; from them comes dew in the dales.'
claims.statement_id: Bait Vafþrúðnismál: "Rimfakse nama kuda yang menarik malam di atas para dewa yang mulia; tetes buih ia jatuhkan setiap pagi; dari situ datang embun di lembah-lembah."
claims.quote: Rimfakse heiter hesten som dreg natt over gjæve gudar; skumdropar han slepper kvar morgon; av det kjem dogg i dalar.

claims.statement: Hrymfaxe means the horse with the rime-covered mane that draws Night's chariot across the sky.
claims.statement_id: Hrymfaxe berarti kuda bersurai berselimut embun beku yang menarik kereta Malam melintasi langit.
claims.quote: Hrymfaxe betyder hesten med rimdækket manke som trækker Nats vogn henover himlen.

claims.statement: K'aǰk' or K'ajk' (Armenian for 'brave') are neutral spirits of the dev group in Armenian mythology.
claims.statement_id: K'aǰk' atau K'ajk' (bahasa Armenia untuk "pemberani") adalah roh netral dari golongan dev dalam mitologi Armenia.
claims.quote: K’aǰk’ bzw. K’ajk’ (armenisch für tapfer) sind in der armenischen Mythologie neutrale Geister aus der Gruppe der Devs.

claims.statement: The K'ajk' live in mountains, caves or gorges and carry out punishments decreed for people; famous are those of Mount Masis (Ararat), who chained Artavazd in a cave after his dead father, King Artašes, cursed him.
claims.statement_id: K'ajk' tinggal di gunung, gua, atau ngarai dan menjalankan hukuman yang ditetapkan bagi manusia; yang terkenal antara lain K'ajk' dari Gunung Masis (Ararat), yang merantai Artavazd di gua setelah ia dikutuk ayahnya yang telah wafat, Raja Artašes.
claims.quote: Die K’ajk’ leben in Bergen, Höhlen oder Schluchten und führen die für Menschen festgesetzten Strafen aus. Bekannt wurden unter anderem die K’ajk’ vom Berg „Masis“ (armenisch für Ararat), die den Artavazd in einer Höhle in Ketten legten, nachdem dieser von seinem toten Vater, dem armenischen König Artašes, verflucht worden war.

claims.statement: Kadzh, kadzhk or kaji (Armenian Քաջք, Georgian ქაჯი) is a spirit of wind, storms and war (дух ветра, бурь и войны) in Armenian and Georgian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Kadzh, kadzhk, atau kaji (Armenia: Քաջք, Georgia: ქაჯი) adalah roh angin, badai, dan perang dalam mitologi Armenia dan Georgia.
claims.quote: Кадж, каджк, или каджи (арм. Քաջք, груз. ქაჯი) — дух ветра, бурь и войны в армянской и грузинской мифологиях.

claims.statement: The name comes from Armenian k'aǰ, 'brave' (храбрый), so it is a euphemism expressing the power ascribed to these spirits.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berasal dari kata Armenia k'aǰ, "pemberani", sehingga nama roh-roh ini merupakan eufemisme yang mengungkapkan kekuatan yang dikaitkan dengan mereka.
claims.quote: Наименование происходит от армянского слова k’aǰ - «храбрый», то есть название духов является эвфемизмом, выражающим могущество, приписываемое этим духам.

claims.statement: By legend, during the Flood Noah had a boy and a girl; after the ark landed on Ararat God asked if he had other children besides Shem, Ham and Japheth, Noah said no, and the two became invisible, founding the race of kaji and peri.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, selama banjir besar Nuh dikaruniai seorang anak lelaki dan perempuan; setelah bahtera berlabuh di Ararat, Tuhan bertanya apakah ia punya anak lain selain Sem, Ham, dan Yafet, Nuh menyangkal, lalu kedua anak itu menjadi tak terlihat dan menurunkan bangsa kaji dan peri.
claims.quote: Согласно легенде, во время потопа у Ноя родились дети: мальчик и девочка. После того, как ковчег причалил к Арарату, Бог спросил Ноя, имеются ли у него ещё дети, кроме Сима, Хама и Яфета, на что Ной ответил отрицательно. Тогда два ребёнка стали невидимыми. От них и пошёл род каджей и пери.

claims.statement: In Armenian folklore the word kadzh often denotes unclean spirits in general (нечисть), whether vishap, chark or other supernatural beings.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Armenia, kata kadzh sering dipakai untuk makhluk halus jahat pada umumnya, entah vishap, chark, atau makhluk gaib lain.
claims.quote: В армянском фольклоре, слово кадж зачастую обозначает нечисть, будь то вишап, чарк и другие сверхъестественные существа.

issues.message: Diusulkan dilewati: Bukan makhluk cerita rakyat tradisional: Krølle-Bølle adalah tokoh troll rekaan modern yang diciptakan Ludvig Mahler pada 1943 untuk putranya dan diterbitkan sebagai buku pada 1948; kini maskot dan merek dagang pulau Bornholm. Kepercayaan rakyat yang melatarinya (Underjordiske) adalah hal yang berbeda. (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kr%C3%B8lle-B%C3%B8lle).

claims.statement: Lutzelfrau, or Lutscherl in eastern Austria and Luz, Luzi or Luzel in the Bavarian Forest, is a witch of German folklore giving apples, nuts and dried plums to children on Saint Lucy's Day (13 December), but with a 'dark Lucia' side said to disembowel or drown naughty children.
claims.statement_id: Lutzelfrau, atau Lutscherl di Austria timur dan Luz, Luzi, atau Luzel di Hutan Bayern, adalah penyihir cerita rakyat Jerman yang memberi apel, kacang, dan prem kering kepada anak-anak pada Hari Santa Lusia (13 Desember), tetapi juga punya sisi "Lusia gelap" yang konon membelah perut atau menenggelamkan anak nakal.
claims.quote: or Lutscherl in Eastern Austria, Luz , Luzi , or Luzel in the Bavarian forest, is a witch in German folklore who gives gifts — particularly apples, nuts and dried plums — to children on Saint Lucy's Day (December 13), but also has a "dark Lucia" side ... This dark, or malevolent Lutzelfrau is reputed to may disembowel (or drown) naughty children

claims.statement: Lutzelfrau is the standard generic name of the tradition in the Alpine areas of Austria and Bavaria, Germany; in parts of Austria she is simply Lucia, and around Burgenland Luzia, Lutzl or Fersenlutzl.
claims.statement_id: Lutzelfrau adalah nama umum tradisi ini di wilayah Alpen Austria dan Bayern, Jerman; di sebagian Austria ia disebut Lucia, dan di sekitar Burgenland Luzia, Lutzl, atau Fersenlutzl.
claims.quote: While Lutzefrau serves as one standardized generic name for the tradition in the Alpine areas of Austria and Bavaria, Germany, in parts of Austria, she is more simply called Lucia . Around Burgenland, she is known as Luzia , Lutzl , or Fersenlutzl .

claims.statement: Lutzelfrau is of course associated with Saint Lucy of Syracuse, and Lucia is a name meaning 'luminous'.
claims.statement_id: Lutzelfrau tentu dikaitkan dengan Santa Lusia dari Sirakusa, dan Lucia adalah nama yang berarti "yang bercahaya".
claims.quote: Lutzelfrau is of course associated with Sankt Lucia (Saint Lucy of Syracuse) and Lucia is a name signifying "luminous" (German: leuchtende ).

claims.statement: In Czechia she is Lucie or Louce, in Slovakia Lucka; Lutzelfrau customs are also common in Slovenia and Croatia, where a 'dark Luz' was contrasted with the Christian saint, and in Slovene she is Lucija.
claims.statement_id: Di Ceko ia dikenal sebagai Lucie atau Louce, di Slowakia Lucka; adat Lutzelfrau juga umum di Slovenia dan Kroasia, tempat "Luz gelap" dikontraskan dengan santa Kristen, dan dalam bahasa Slovenia ia disebut Lucija.
claims.quote: In Czechia, she is known as Lucie or Louce , etc. In Slovakia, she is called Lucka . Lutzelfrau customs are also common in Slovenia and Croatia, where a "dark Luz" was contrasted to the Christian saint. In Slovene, she is called Lucija .

claims.statement: In Burgenland the Lutzelfrau or Pudlfrau visits children on St Lucy's day and 'tosses' sweets through the doorway.
claims.statement_id: Di Burgenland, Lutzelfrau atau Pudlfrau mengunjungi anak-anak pada hari Santa Lusia dan "menggulirkan" manisan lewat ambang pintu.
claims.quote: In Burgenland, Lutzelfrau or Pudlfrau visits the children on St. Lucia's day and "tosses (pudelt ) sweets through the doorway.

claims.statement: Lutzelfrau is a witch of German folklore said to fly at night on her broom, who gives apples, nuts and dried plums to children on Saint Lucy's day (13 December).
claims.statement_id: Lutzelfrau adalah penyihir cerita rakyat Jerman yang konon terbang di malam hari dengan sapunya dan memberi apel, kacang, dan prem kering kepada anak-anak pada hari raya Santa Lusia (13 Desember).
claims.quote: Lutzelfrau est une sorcière du folklore allemand qui volerait la nuit sur son balai, elle offre des cadeaux - en particulier des pommes, des noix et des prunes séchées - aux enfants le jour de la fête de Sainte-Lucie ( 13 décembre ).

claims.statement: According to a mid-19th-century source the Lucia of Bohemia and Tyrol appeared as a goat draped in a bedsheet with horns poking out, paralleled in Scandinavia.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sumber pertengahan abad ke-19, Lusia di Bohemia dan Tirol tampil sebagai kambing yang berselubung seprai dengan tanduk mencuat, dan hal serupa ada di Skandinavia.
claims.quote: According to a mid-19th century source, the Lucia of Bohemia and Tyrol appeared as a goat, draped in a bedsheet with horns protruding out of the sheet. This is paralleled in Scandinavia.

claims.statement: Night ravens (Danish/Norwegian nattravn; Swedish nattramn, nattkorp; German Nachtkrapp, Nachtrabe) are creatures of European folklore, mostly raven-like beings appearing at night; the lore differs regionally, they may be other beings such as undead shapeshifted into ravens, and they are sometimes bugbears in cautionary tales.
claims.statement_id: Gagak malam (Denmark/Norwegia: nattravn; Swedia: nattramn, nattkorp; Jerman: Nachtkrapp, Nachtrabe) adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Eropa yang umumnya digambarkan mirip gagak dan muncul di malam hari; ceritanya berbeda menurut daerah, gagak malam bisa juga makhluk lain seperti mayat hidup yang berubah menjadi gagak, dan kadang dipakai sebagai momok dalam kisah peringatan.
claims.quote: Danish and Norwegian: nattravn ; Swedish: nattramn , nattkorp ; German: Nachtkrapp , Nachtrabe ) are creatures of European folklore, predominantly described as raven like creatures appearing in the night. The folklore differs regionally, and night ravens may be other beings, such as undead, shapeshifted into ravens.

claims.statement: In German folklore, mainly southern Germany and Austria, the night raven leaves its hiding place at night to hunt; if seen by small children it carries them to its nest and devours them, while other legends say it merely bags them and takes them away.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, terutama Jerman selatan dan Austria, gagak malam keluar dari persembunyiannya di malam hari untuk berburu; bila dilihat anak kecil, ia menculik mereka ke sarangnya dan memangsanya, sedangkan legenda lain menyebut ia hanya memasukkan anak ke karungnya dan membawanya pergi.
claims.quote: In German folklore (German: Nachtkrapp , Nachtrabe ), mainly of Southern Germany and Austria, the most common legends claim that the night raven leaves its hiding place at night to hunt. If it is seen by little children, it will abduct them into its nest and messily devour them ... According to other legends, the night raven will merely put children in his bag and take them away.

claims.statement: There is a version called the Guter Nachtkrapp, the 'good night raven'.
claims.statement_id: Ada versi yang disebut Guter Nachtkrapp, "gagak malam yang baik".
claims.quote: The Guter Nachtkrapp (German, literal translation

claims.statement: Nachtkrabb or Nacht(t)rapp is, in southern Germany and Austria, the name of a child-frightening figure with a function like the Sandman's; it supposedly snatches children still outdoors after dark, and its Franconian counterpart is the Nachtgiger.
claims.statement_id: Nachtkrabb atau Nacht(t)rapp di Jerman selatan dan Austria adalah nama momok penakut anak dengan fungsi serupa Sandmann; ia konon menyambar anak yang masih di luar setelah gelap, dan padanannya di Franken disebut Nachtgiger.
claims.quote: Nachtkrabb oder Nacht(t)rapp ist im süddeutschen und österreichischen Raum der Name einer Kinderschreckfigur, die eine ähnliche Funktion wie der Sandmann erfüllt. Der Nachtkrabb greift sich angeblich Kinder, die sich nach Einbruch der Dunkelheit noch im Freien aufhalten ... Das fränkische Pendant nennt sich Nachtgiger.

claims.statement: Krabb (also Krapp, Krabbe, Rappe; from Old High German [h]raban) in Upper German dialects means raven or other corvids; these carrion birds were readily credited with baleful deeds, such as the raven stealing children at night.
claims.statement_id: Krabb (juga Krapp, Krabbe, Rappe; dari Jerman Hulu Kuno [h]raban) dalam dialek Jerman Hulu berarti gagak atau burung sejenis; burung pemakan bangkai ini mudah dikaitkan dengan berbagai pengaruh buruk, misalnya menculik anak di malam hari.
claims.quote: Krabb (auch Krapp, Krabbe, Grabbe, Rappe, von ahd. [h]raban) ist in oberdeutschen Dialekten eine Bezeichnung für den Raben oder andere Rabenvögel. Es lag nahe, dass diesen aasfressenden Schwarmvögeln auch allerhand unheilbringende Wirkung angedichtet wurde, zum Beispiel, dass der Rabe nachts die Kinder entführe.

claims.statement: In central Thuringia children are warned of night ravens that always come in flocks and catch children not home after dark.
claims.statement_id: Di Thüringen tengah anak-anak diperingatkan tentang gagak malam yang selalu datang berkawanan dan menangkap anak yang belum pulang setelah gelap.
claims.quote: In Zentralthüringen werden Kinder vor den Nachtraben gewarnt, die stets im Schwarm auftreten und Kinder fingen und mitnähmen, die nach Einbruch der Dunkelheit nicht zuhause sind.

claims.statement: They are sometimes used as a bugbear in cautionary tales to scare children into going to bed.
claims.statement_id: Gagak malam kadang dipakai sebagai momok dalam kisah peringatan untuk menakuti anak-anak agar mau tidur.
claims.quote: They are sometimes used as a bugbear creature of cautionary tales, used to scare children into going to bed.

claims.statement: Nis Puk (also Niß Puk) is a legendary kobold-like creature from Danish-, Low German- and North Frisian-speaking northern Germany and southern Denmark, including Schleswig; in Denmark it is also nis pug, a variant of the nisse.
claims.statement_id: Nis Puk (juga Niß Puk) adalah makhluk legenda sejenis kobold dari wilayah berbahasa Denmark, Jerman Rendah, dan Frisia Utara di Jerman utara dan Denmark selatan, termasuk Schleswig; di Denmark ia juga disebut nis pug, varian nisse.
claims.quote: The Nis Puk (sometimes also Niß Puk ( German: [ˈnɪs pʊk] )) is a legendary creature, a kind of Kobold, from Danish-, Low German- and North Frisian-speaking areas of Northern Germany and Southern Denmark, among them Schleswig, today divided into the German Southern Schleswig and Danish Northern Schleswig. It is also known in Denmark itself as nis pug , as a variant of nisse.

claims.statement: Depending on place, it may appear as a domestic spirit or take the role of what Danish and German mythology call a Drak or kobold, an infernal spirit enriching its owner with stolen goods.
claims.statement_id: Tergantung tempatnya, ia bisa tampil sebagai roh rumah tangga atau berperan sebagai makhluk yang disebut Drak atau kobold dalam mitologi Denmark dan Jerman, roh dari neraka yang membuat pemiliknya kaya dengan membawakan barang curian.
claims.quote: Depending on the place, it can either appear as a domestic spirit or take on the role of a being generally called Drak or Kobold in Danish and German mythology, an infernal spirit making its owner wealthy by bringing them stolen goods.

claims.statement: The form Nis Puk is called a 'tautological juxtaposition' of two words meaning the same: Niß said to come from Nikolaus, and Puk attested as Old Danish puge, from Old Norse púki, 'kobold'.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk Nis Puk disebut "penjajaran tautologis" dua kata bermakna sama: Niß konon dari nama Nikolaus, dan Puk tercatat dalam bahasa Denmark Kuno puge, dari Nordik Kuno púki, "kobold".
claims.quote: The form Nis Puk is described as a "tautological juxtaposition" of two words meaning the same thing. The name Niß said to be derived from the proper name Nikolaus, i.e., Nicholas ... The name Puk is attested in the Old Danish form puge , descended from Old Norse puki púke , meaning kobold

claims.statement: Nis Puk looks after house, yard and animals; he lives in the attic or barn, unseen by adults, and once a year at Christmas must get a bowl of porridge with butter, or he moves to another village.
claims.statement_id: Nis Puk menjaga rumah, halaman, dan ternak; ia tinggal di loteng atau lumbung, tak terlihat oleh orang dewasa, dan setahun sekali saat Natal harus diberi semangkuk bubur bermentega, bila tidak ia pindah ke desa lain.
claims.quote: Der Nis Puk soll auf Haus, Hof und Tiere achtgeben ... Der Nis Puk soll auf dem Dachboden oder in einer Scheune leben. Angeblich können ihn Erwachsene nicht mehr sehen. Einmal im Jahr, zu Weihnachten, muss dem Nis Puk eine Schüssel Grütze (mit Butter) gebracht werden. Geschieht das nicht, wandert der Nis Puk in ein anderes Dorf.

claims.statement: Nis Puk (Sylt Frisian Nes Pük; Danish Nis Pug, Nis Puge) is a folk-tale figure, and a small statue of him stands in front of the school in Neukirchen.
claims.statement_id: Nis Puk (Frisia Sylt: Nes Pük; Denmark: Nis Pug, Nis Puge) adalah tokoh dongeng rakyat, dan di depan sekolah Neukirchen berdiri patung kecil Nis Puk.
claims.quote: Nis Puk (im Sylter Friesisch Nes Pük, im Dänischen zum Teil auch Nis Pug und Nis Puge) ist eine Figur aus dem Bereich der Volksmärchen. ... Vor der Schule in Neukirchen befindet sich eine kleine Statue von Nis Puk.

claims.statement: The figure combines the Danish-Scanian-Norwegian nisse with the English puk; he looks after house and animals if the occupants treat their own children and animals well; without porridge the house faces decay and misfortune; a Sylt saying runs 'Hi glüüret üs en pük' (he stares like a Nis Puk), and he features in Boy Lornsen's children's books.
claims.statement_id: Figur ini memadukan nisse Denmark-Skåne-Norwegia dengan puk Inggris; ia menjaga rumah dan hewan bila penghuni bersedia memperlakukan anak dan hewan mereka dengan baik; tanpa bubur rumah itu terancam kerusakan dan malapetaka; pepatah Sylt berbunyi "Hi glüüret üs en pük" (ia menatap seperti Nis Puk), dan ia muncul dalam buku-buku anak Boy Lornsen.
claims.quote: Figuren forbinder den dansk-skånsk-norske nisse med den engelske puk ... Han tager sig af huset og dyrene, hvis beboerne er villige til at behandle deres egne børn og dyr godt. ... Huset ville så være udsat for forfald og ulykker. ... Et ordsprog fra øen Sild siger på sildfrisisk Hi glüüret üs en pük (≈Han stirrer som en Nis Puk). Figuren fandt indgang i flere af Boy Lornsens børnebøger.

claims.statement: Rå, short for rådare ('ruler'), from råda ('to rule, to advise') and Old Norse ráða, is a spirit keeping a particular place or landform, known in both Nordic and Sami culture, where it is called radie.
claims.statement_id: Rå, kependekan dari rådare ("penguasa"), dari råda ("memerintah, menasihati") dan Nordik Kuno ráða, adalah roh penjaga suatu tempat atau bentang alam, dikenal dalam budaya Nordik maupun Sami, yang menyebutnya radie.
claims.quote: short for rådare ("ruler") from råda (to rule, to advise) from old Norse ráða, is a spirit who is the keeper or warden of a particular location or landform. The rå is known both in Nordic culture and in the Sami culture, where it is called radie.

claims.statement: It was important for people to keep good relations with them, as they ruled the natural forces and animals in their care and could bring good or bad luck to anyone interfering with what they watched over.
claims.statement_id: Manusia penting menjaga hubungan baik dengan mereka, karena mereka menguasai kekuatan alam dan hewan di bawah asuhannya dan dapat membawa untung maupun sial bagi orang yang mengganggu tempat dan makhluk yang dijaganya.
claims.quote: It was important for humans to cultivate good relationships with them, since they had power over the natural forces and animals under their care, and could cause both good and bad luck for humans who interfered with the places and creatures under their watch.

claims.statement: The kinds of rår are sometimes told apart by their sphere of nature, such as skogsrå or hulder (forest), sjörå (fresh water), havsrå (salt water) and bergsrå (mountains).
claims.statement_id: Jenis-jenis rår kadang dibedakan menurut wilayah alam yang dikaitkan dengannya, seperti skogsrå atau hulder (hutan), sjörå (air tawar), havsrå (air asin), dan bergsrå (gunung).
claims.quote: The different species of rår are sometimes distinguished according to the different spheres of nature with which each was associated, such as skogsrå or hulder (forest), sjörå (freshwater) or havsrå (saltwater), and bergsrå (mountains).

claims.statement: Rå (plural rår) is a Swedish word; these beings also exist in Sami culture, where they are called radie.
claims.statement_id: Rå (jamak rår) adalah kata Swedia; makhluk ini juga ada dalam budaya Sami, tempat ia disebut radie.
claims.quote: Rå (pluriel : rår) est un mot suédois ; ces êtres sont aussi présents dans la culture sami, où ils sont appelés radie.

claims.statement: Every object, animal or plant had its own protecting rå, and a rå could also protect human places and things, such as the skeppsrået (ship's rå) or gruvrået (mine's rå).
claims.statement_id: Setiap benda, hewan, atau tumbuhan punya rå pelindungnya sendiri, dan rå juga dapat melindungi tempat dan benda milik manusia, seperti skeppsrået (rå kapal) atau gruvrået (rå tambang).
claims.quote: Chaque objet, animal ou plante avait son propre rå qui le protégeait. Un rå pouvait également avoir un pouvoir de protection sur des lieux et des objets appartenant à des humains, comme le skeppsrået (rå du bateau) ou le gruvrået (rå de la mine).

claims.statement: Rår may appear as animals or as a man or woman; the skogsrå and bergsrå are usually described as female.
claims.statement_id: Rår bisa tampil berwujud hewan atau sebagai laki-laki atau perempuan; skogsrå dan bergsrå biasanya digambarkan perempuan.
claims.quote: Les rår peuvent apparaître sous forme animale ou sous la forme d'un homme ou d'une femme ; le skogsrå et le bergsrå sont généralement décrits comme féminins.

claims.statement: The Roggenmuhme is a female grain demon and children's bugbear of German legend who keeps to field and acre.
claims.statement_id: Roggenmuhme adalah roh gandum perempuan dan momok penakut anak dalam sage Jerman yang tinggal di ladang.
claims.quote: Die Roggenmuhme ist ein weiblicher Korndämon und Kinderschreck der deutschen Sage, der sich im Feld und Acker aufhält.

claims.statement: The Roggenmuhme walks the field, feeds on grain and pulls out unripe ears; angry with a farmer she withers his field, but generally her passage brings fertility; at harvest she flees into the last sheaf and also receives a share of the crop.
claims.statement_id: Roggenmuhme berjalan mondar-mandir di ladang, makan biji-bijian, dan mencabut bulir yang belum matang; bila marah kepada petani ia mengeringkan ladangnya, tetapi umumnya langkahnya membawa kesuburan; saat panen ia melarikan diri ke berkas terakhir, dan ia juga diberi bagian panen.
claims.quote: Die Roggenmuhme geht im Feld auf und ab, ernährt sich vom Korn und reißt die unreifen Ähren aus. Wenn sie dem Bauer zürnt, so dorrt sie sein Feld aus und straft ihn auf diese Weise. Allgemein sorgt das Durchschreiten des Feldes durch die Roggenmuhme allerdings für Fruchtbarkeit. Bei der Ernte flieht sie in die letzte Garbe. Die Roggenmuhme erhält auch einen Anteil an der Ernte

claims.statement: Her dwelling is imagined underground, in a 'root realm' or cave; like Frau Holle and Perchta she punishes lazy maids who leave their distaffs unspun in the Twelve Nights, hence also Rockenmör; her breath brings sickness and death.
claims.statement_id: Tempat tinggal Roggenmuhme dibayangkan di bawah tanah, di "kerajaan akar" atau gua; seperti Frau Holle dan Perchta ia menghukum pelayan malas yang tidak menyelesaikan pintalan pada dua belas malam, sehingga disebut juga Rockenmör; napasnya membawa penyakit dan kematian.
claims.quote: Die Wohnung der Roggenmuhme wird unterirdisch gedacht, im „Wurzelreich“ oder in einer Höhle. Die Roggenmuhme ähnelt Frau Holle und Perchta darin, dass sie die faulen Mägde straft, welche in den Zwölfnächten ihre Spinnrocken nicht abgesponnen haben. Daher heißt sie auch Rockenmör. Der Hauch der Roggenmuhme bringt Krankheit und Tod.

claims.statement: Names in Roggen- recorded for the Roggenmuhme include Roggenmutter, Roggenfrau, Roggenweib, Roggenalte and Roggenhexe.
claims.statement_id: Nama berunsur Roggen- yang tercatat untuk Roggenmuhme antara lain Roggenmutter, Roggenfrau, Roggenweib, Roggenalte, dan Roggenhexe.
claims.quote: Folgende Namen auf Roggen- sind für die Roggenmuhme außerdem überliefert: Roggenmutter, Roggenfrau, Roggenweib, Roggenweibchen, Roggenwief, Roggenalte, Roggenhexe

claims.statement: Names with Korn- include Kornmutter, Kornmoder, Kornmuhme, Kornfrau and Kornweib.
claims.statement_id: Nama berunsur Korn- misalnya Kornmutter, Kornmoder, Kornmuhme, Kornfrau, dan Kornweib.
claims.quote: Namen mit dem Element Korn- sind beispielsweise: Kornmutter, Kornmoder, Kornmuhme, Kornmöhm, Kornmähne, Kornfrau, Kornweib

claims.statement: The 'rye woman' (Lithuanian Rugių bóba, Serbian Baba Ruga, German Roggenmuhme) is a figure of Slavic, Germanic and Baltic mythology linked with field, bread and rye (поле, хлеб, рожь), named as a spirit or deity.
claims.statement_id: Perempuan gandum hitam (Lituania: Rugių bóba; Serbia: Baba Ruga; Jerman: Roggenmuhme) adalah tokoh mitologi Slavia, Jermanik, dan Baltik yang terkait dengan ladang, roti, dan gandum hitam, disebut sebagai roh atau dewi.
claims.quote: Ржаная баба (лит. Rugių ̃ bóba, серб. Баба Руга, Баба Рога, нем. Roggenmuhme) – персонаж славянской, германской и балтской мифологии, связанный с полем, хлебом и рожью. Упоминается как дух или божество.

claims.statement: In Norse mythology Skinfaxi and Hrímfaxi are the horses of Dagr (day) and Nótt (night); the names mean 'shining mane' and 'frost mane', and Skinfaxi pulls Dagr's chariot across the sky every day, its mane lighting sky and earth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Skinfaxi dan Hrímfaxi adalah kuda Dagr (siang) dan Nótt (malam); namanya berarti "surai bersinar" dan "surai berembun beku", dan Skinfaxi menarik kereta Dagr melintasi langit setiap hari sementara suainya menerangi langit dan bumi.
claims.quote: In Norse mythology, Skinfaxi (Old Norse: [ˈskinˌfɑkse] ) and Hrímfaxi [ˈhriːmˌfɑkse] are the horses of Dagr (day) and Nótt (night). The names Skinfaxi and Hrímfaxi mean "shining mane" and "frost mane", respectively. Skinfaxi pulls Dagr's chariot across the sky every day and his mane lights up the sky and earth below.

claims.statement: Skinfaxe (Old Norse Skinfaxi, 'shining mane') is the horse harnessed to Dag's chariot in Norse mythology, driven across the sky each day; its mane and tail shine like gold and light up the world.
claims.statement_id: Skinfaxe (Nordik Kuno Skinfaxi, "surai bersinar") adalah kuda yang ditambatkan pada kereta Dag dalam mitologi Nordik dan dikendarai melintasi langit setiap hari; surai dan ekornya bersinar seperti emas dan menerangi dunia.
claims.quote: Skinfaxe (Oldnordisk: Skinfaxi, 'skinnende manke') er hesten, der i nordisk mytologi er forspændt Dags vogn. Han bliver på denne kørt hen over himlen hver dag. Hestens manke og hale skinner som guld og oplyser verden.

claims.statement: Skinfakse (Old Norse Skinfaxi, 'shining mane') is the horse Day rides across the sky daily; the Gylfaginning of the Younger Edda says: 'The horse Dag has is called Skinfakse, and light shines over all the air and earth from his mane.'
claims.statement_id: Skinfakse (Nordik Kuno Skinfaxi, "surai bersinar") adalah kuda yang ditunggangi Dag melintasi langit setiap hari; dalam Gylfaginning di Den yngre Edda disebut: "Kuda milik Dag bernama Skinfakse, dan cahaya memancar ke seluruh udara dan bumi dari suainya."
claims.quote: Skinfakse (Norrønt: Skinfaxi, skinnende man) er i norrøn mytologi den hesten Dag rir på over himmelen hver dag. Skinfakse nevnes i Gylvaginning i Den yngre Edda: Den hesten Dag har heiter Skinfakse og det lyser over all lufta og jorda frå fakset hans

claims.statement: Oehlenschläger's poem Guldhornene mentions the sky horses: black Hrymfaxe sinks into the sea, Delling opens the gates of morning, and Skinfaxe trots forth.
claims.statement_id: Puisi Oehlenschläger Guldhornene menyebut kuda-kuda langit: Hrymfaxe yang hitam menyelam ke laut, Delling membuka gerbang pagi, dan Skinfaxe pun berderap.
claims.quote: Oehlenschlägers digt Guldhornene omtaler himmelhestene: "Hrymfaxe den sorte puster og dukker og i Havet sig begraver. Morgenens Porte Delling oplukker, og Skinfaxe traver

claims.statement: The horse Hrymfaxe is harnessed to the chariot that carries the moon across the sky at night.
claims.statement_id: Kuda Hrymfaxe ditambatkan pada kereta yang membawa bulan melintasi langit di malam hari.
claims.quote: Hesten Hrymfaxe er forspændt vognen, der bærer månen over himlen om natten.

claims.statement: In this translated Edda poem, Skinfaxi is the steed who draws the glittering day for men; he seems the best of horses to heroes, and his mane burns brightly.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan puisi Edda ini, Skinfaxi adalah kuda yang menarik siang yang berkilau bagi manusia; bagi para pahlawan ia tampak sebagai kuda terbaik, dan suainya menyala terang.
claims.quote: Skinfaxi is he, the steed who for men The glittering day doth draw; The best of horses to heroes he seems, And brightly his mane doth burn.

claims.statement: Hrimfaxi is the steed that brings night for the noble gods; each morning foam falls from his bit and becomes the dews in the dales.
claims.statement_id: Hrimfaxi adalah kuda yang membawa malam bagi para dewa mulia; tiap pagi buih jatuh dari kekangnya dan menjadi embun di lembah.
claims.quote: Hrimfaxi name they the steed that anew Brings night for the noble gods; Each morning foam from his bit there falls, And thence come the dews in the dales.

claims.statement: All-father gave Night and Day, her son, two horses and two cars and set them in the heavens to drive in turn round the world, each for twelve hours.
claims.statement_id: All-father memberi Malam dan Siang, putranya, dua kuda dan dua kereta, lalu menempatkan mereka di langit agar bergantian berkeliling dunia, masing-masing dua belas jam.
claims.quote: Then took All-father, Night, and Day, her son, and gave them two horses and two cars, and set them up in the heavens that they might drive successively one after the other, each in twelve hours' time, round the world.

claims.statement: The horse Day uses is named Skinfaxi, from whose mane light is shed over the earth and the heavens.
claims.statement_id: Kuda yang dipakai Siang bernama Skinfaxi; dari suainya cahaya memancar ke bumi dan langit.
claims.quote: The horse made use of by Day is named Skinfaxi, from whose mane is shed light over the earth and the heavens.

claims.statement: Night then married Delling of the Æsir race, and their son was Day (Dagr), a child light and beautiful like his father.
claims.statement_id: Malam kemudian menikah dengan Delling dari bangsa Æsir, dan putra mereka adalah Siang (Dagr), anak yang terang dan elok seperti ayahnya.
claims.quote: She then espoused Delling, of the Æsir race, and their son was Day, (Dagr) a child light and beauteous like his father.

claims.statement: The translator's note says Glath ("Joyous") is identified in the Skaldskaparmal with Skinfaxi, the horse of the day.
claims.statement_id: Catatan penerjemah menyebut Glath ("Gembira") dalam Skaldskaparmal diidentifikasi dengan Skinfaxi, kuda sang siang.
claims.quote: Glath ("Joyous"): identified in the Skaldskaparmal with Skinfaxi, the horse of the day; cf. Vafthruthnismol, 12.

claims.statement: The translator's notes gloss Skinfaxi as "Shining-Mane" and Hrimfaxi as "Frosty-Mane".
claims.statement_id: Catatan penerjemah mengartikan Skinfaxi sebagai "Surai Bersinar" dan Hrimfaxi sebagai "Surai Berembun beku".
claims.quote: Skinfaxi: "Shining-Mane." ... Hrimfaxi: "Frosty-Mane."

claims.statement: Slattenpatten or slattenlangpat (literally 'flaccid breasts' or 'saggy long breast') is a female creature of Danish folklore.
claims.statement_id: Slattenpatten atau slattenlangpat (harfiah "payudara kendur" atau "payudara panjang yang melorot") adalah makhluk perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Denmark.
claims.quote: Slattenpatten or slattenlangpat (literally “flaccid-breasts” or “saggy-long-breast”, is a female creature in Danish folklore.

claims.statement: Legend says Kong Volmer chased and shot her every night, only to see her return the next morning.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Kong Volmer mengejar dan menembaknya setiap malam, tetapi ia kembali keesokan paginya.
claims.quote: The legend goes that Kong Volmer chased and shot her every night, only to see her return the next morning

claims.statement: Slattenpatten or Slattenlangpat is a female being of Danish folk belief, especially tied to Suså; also called ellekvinde, ellekone or elverkone, and unlike the usually very beautiful ellepige she is marked by extraordinarily long breasts.
claims.statement_id: Slattenpatten atau Slattenlangpat adalah makhluk perempuan dalam kepercayaan rakyat Denmark, terutama dikaitkan dengan Suså; ia juga disebut ellekvinde, ellekone, atau elverkone, dan berbeda dari ellepige yang biasanya sangat cantik, ia dicirikan payudara yang amat panjang.
claims.quote: Slattenpatten eller Slattenlangpat er et kvindeligt væsen i dansk folketro, især knyttet til Suså. Væsnet betegnes også som en ellekvinde, ellekone eller elverkone. I modsætning til en ellepige, der i reglen beskrives som meget smuk, er Slattenpatten karakteriseret ved at have overordentligt lange bryster.

claims.statement: Her breasts hang down to the waist but can be thrown over the shoulder so a child on her back can feed, and when chased she flings them over her shoulders; in southern Zealand legends tell of her being hunted by 'Kong Volmer' (really Valdemar Atterdag) or 'Wojens Jæger' with hounds.
claims.statement_id: Payudaranya menjuntai sampai ke pinggang tetapi dapat dilempar ke bahu agar anak di punggung dapat menyusu, dan saat dikejar ia melempar payudara ke bahunya; di Sjælland selatan ada sejumlah legenda ia diburu "Kong Volmer" (sebenarnya Valdemar Atterdag) atau "Wojens Jæger" dengan anjing-anjingnya.
claims.quote: Brysterne hænger "helt ned til bæltestedet", men de kan kastes op over skulderen, således at et barn kan die, selvom det bæres på ryggen. I situationer, hvor Slattenpatten jages, slænger hun blot brysterne over skuldrene ... På Sydsjælland findes en række sagn, hvor Slattenpatten jages af "Kong Volmer" (egentlig Valdemar Atterdag) eller "Wojens Jæger" med sine hunde.

claims.statement: Slattenpatten steals from people at night, but cannot steal bread scored with a cross; those she pursues can escape by running across plough furrows, since she can only run along furrows cut with a steel plough, or by jumping over running water.
claims.statement_id: Slattenpatten mencuri dari manusia di malam hari, tetapi tak bisa mencuri roti yang digoresi salib; orang yang dikejarnya bisa lolos dengan berlari menyeberangi alur bajak, karena ia hanya bisa berlari searah alur yang dibajak dengan bajak baja, atau dengan melompati air mengalir.
claims.quote: Slattenpatten røver fra menneskene om natten. Men ridses et kors i ens brød og bagværk, kan hun ikke stjæle det. Følger hun efter én, kan man undslippe hende ved at løbe ud over markerne og tværs over plovfurerne, for hun kan kun løbe langs med furerne, når de er pløjet med stålplov. ... Man kan også hoppe over rindende vand

claims.statement: Another legend says her breasts were long so she could suckle her fish-children under water; slattenlangpat is therefore also linked with water and considered a water goddess, especially in Zealand according to some archaeologists.
claims.statement_id: Legenda lain menyebut payudaranya panjang agar ia bisa menyusui anak-anak ikannya di bawah air; karena itu slattenlangpat juga dikaitkan dengan air dan dianggap dewi air, khususnya di Sjælland menurut sebagian arkeolog.
claims.quote: Another legend tells us that her breasts were so long so that she could breastfeed her fish-children under the water. Slattenlangpat is therefore also associated with water and considered a water goddess, in particular according to certain archaeologists, in the Danish region of Zealand.

claims.statement: In the 2010 renovation of Axeltorv in Næstved, the old fountain was replaced by a statue of Slattenpatten by Bjørn Nørgaard.
claims.statement_id: Dalam renovasi Axeltorv di Næstved pada 2010, air mancur lama diganti patung Slattenpatten karya Bjørn Nørgaard.
claims.quote: I forbindelse med renovering af Axeltorv i Næstved blev det hidtidige springvand i 2010 erstattet af en statue af Slattenpatten, udført af Bjørn Nørgaard.

claims.statement: Tanngrisnir and Tanngnjóstr are the goats that pull the god Thor's chariot in Norse mythology, attested in the Poetic Edda, compiled in the 13th century from older tradition, and in the Prose Edda written by Snorri Sturluson in the 13th century.
claims.statement_id: Tanngrisnir dan Tanngnjóstr adalah kambing jantan penarik kereta dewa Thor dalam mitologi Nordik, tercatat dalam Edda Puisi yang dihimpun abad ke-13 dari tradisi lebih tua dan dalam Edda Prosa yang ditulis Snorri Sturluson pada abad ke-13.
claims.quote: and Tanngnjóstr ([ˈtɑnːˌɡnjoːstz̠] ) are the goats who pull the chariot of the god Thor in Norse mythology. They are attested in the Poetic Edda, compiled in the 13th century from earlier traditional sources, and the Prose Edda, written by Snorri Sturluson in the 13th century.

claims.statement: Old Norse Tanngrisnir means 'teeth-barer, snarler' and Tanngnjóstr 'teeth-grinder, teeth-gnasher'; Rudolf Simek says the names were young when recorded and may be Snorri's inventions; Tanngnjóstr is sometimes anglicised Tanngiost.
claims.statement_id: Nama Nordik Kuno Tanngrisnir berarti "penyeringai gigi, penggeram" dan Tanngnjóstr "penggeretak gigi"; Rudolf Simek menilai nama-nama ini masih muda saat dicatat dan mungkin rekaan Snorri; Tanngnjóstr kadang ditulis Tanngiost dalam bahasa Inggris modern.
claims.quote: The Old Norse name Tanngrisnir translates to "teeth-barer, snarler" and Tanngnjóstr to "teeth-grinder, teeth-gnasher". Scholar Rudolf Simek comments that the names were young when recorded, and may have been inventions of Snorri. Tanngnjóstr is sometimes modernly anglicized as Tanngiost.

claims.statement: The Prose Edda says that when Thor cooks the goats their flesh feeds the god, and after he revives them with his hammer Mjölnir they live again the next day.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Edda Prosa, daging kambing yang dimasak Thor menjadi santapan sang dewa, dan setelah dibangkitkan dengan palu Mjölnir mereka hidup kembali keesokan harinya.
claims.quote: The Prose Edda relates that when Thor cooks the goats, their flesh provides sustenance for the god, and, after Thor resurrects them with his hammer, Mjölnir, they are brought back to life the next day.

claims.statement: The names mean 'grinding the teeth, tooth-gnasher', from Old Norse tann ('tooth') and gnjóstr from the verb gnísta ('to rub together'), read as imitating the sound of jagged lightning, as Thor's moving chariot sounds as thunder.
claims.statement_id: Nama-nama ini berarti "menggeretakkan gigi, penggeretak gigi", dari Nordik Kuno tann ("gigi") dan gnjóstr dari kata kerja gnísta ("menggesek"), dan ditafsirkan sebagai tiruan bunyi petir yang menyambar bergerigi, sejalan dengan bunyi kereta Thor sebagai guntur.
claims.quote: Die Namen bedeuten übersetzt: „Mit den Zähnen knirschend, Zahnknirscher“, aus dem altnordischen „Tann“ für Zahn und „gnjóstr“ vom Verb „gnísta“ für aneinanderreiben. ... Die Namen werden dahin gedeutet, dass sie lautmalend das Geräusch des in Zacken niederfahrenden Blitzes nachahmen, analog zum lautmalenden Geräusch durch den fahrenden Wagen Thors als der Donner

claims.statement: One of the farmer's children, Þjálfi, broke a bone to suck the marrow, leaving one goat lame on revival, so Thor keeps Þjálfi and his sister Röskva as servants.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu anak petani, Þjálfi, mematahkan tulang untuk mengisap sumsumnya sehingga satu kambing pincang setelah dibangkitkan, dan karena itu Thor menjadikan Þjálfi dan saudarinya Röskva pelayannya.
claims.quote: one of their children, Þjálfi, broke one of the bones to suck out the marrow, resulting in the lameness of one of the goats upon resurrection. As a result, Thor maintains Þjálfi and his sister Röskva as his servants.

claims.statement: Scholars link the ever-replenishing goats to Sæhrímnir, eaten nightly in Norse mythology, and to Scandinavian folk beliefs about herring bones and witchcraft.
claims.statement_id: Para sarjana mengaitkan kambing yang terus pulih ini dengan Sæhrímnir yang disantap setiap malam dalam mitologi Nordik dan dengan kepercayaan rakyat Skandinavia tentang tulang ikan haring dan sihir.
claims.quote: Scholars have linked the ever-replenishing goats to the nightly-consumed beast Sæhrímnir in Norse mythology and Scandinavian folk beliefs involving herring bones and witchcraft.

claims.statement: Gylfaginning chapter 21: 'Thor owns two goats, Tanngnióstr and Tanngrisnir.'
claims.statement_id: Gylfaginning bab 21: "Thor memiliki dua kambing jantan, Tanngnióstr dan Tanngrisnir."
claims.quote: „Þórr á hafra ii er svá heita: Tanngnióstr ok Tanngrisnir ...“ „Þórr besitzt zwei Böcke Tanngnióstr und Tanngrisnir ...“

claims.quote: Tanngrisnir ( Old Norse: [ˈtɑnːˌɡrisnez̠] ) and Tanngnjóstr ([ˈtɑnːˌɡnjoːstz̠] ) are the goats who pull the chariot of the god Thor in Norse mythology. They are attested in the Poetic Edda, compiled in the 13th century from earlier traditional sources, and the Prose Edda

claims.statement: Old Norse Tanngrisnir translates as 'teeth-barer, snarler' and Tanngnjóstr as 'teeth-grinder, teeth-gnasher'.
claims.statement_id: Nama Nordik Kuno Tanngrisnir diterjemahkan "penyeringai gigi, penggeram", sedangkan Tanngnjóstr "penggeretak gigi".
claims.quote: The Old Norse name Tanngrisnir translates to "teeth-barer, snarler" and Tanngnjóstr to "teeth-grinder, teeth-gnasher".

claims.statement: The Prose Edda says that when Thor cooks the goats their flesh feeds the god, and after he revives them with Mjölnir they live again next day.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Edda Prosa, daging kambing yang dimasak Thor menjadi santapan sang dewa, dan setelah dibangkitkan dengan Mjölnir mereka hidup kembali keesokan harinya.
claims.quote: The Prose Edda relates that when Thor cooks the goats, their flesh provides sustenance for the god, and, after Thor resurrects them with his hammer, Mjölnir, they are brought back to life the next day.

claims.statement: Tanngnióstr (tooth-gnasher) and Tanngrisnir (teeth-barer), also known as Thor's goats, are the billy goats drawing Thor's chariot in Norse mythology; Tanngrisnir is also translated 'tooth-gnasher' or 'gap-toothed' (Auseinanderstehende Zähne).
claims.statement_id: Tanngnióstr (penggeretak gigi) dan Tanngrisnir (penyeringai gigi), dikenal juga sebagai kambing-kambing Thor, adalah kambing jantan yang menarik kereta Thor dalam mitologi Nordik; Tanngrisnir juga diterjemahkan "penggeretak gigi" atau "bergigi renggang".
claims.quote: Tanngnióstr (Zähneknirscher) und Tanngrisnir (Zähneblecker) auch als Thors Böcke bekannt, sind in der Nordischen Mythologie Thors Ziegenböcke, die dessen Wagen ziehen. ... Tanngrisnir wird ebenfalls übersetzt mit Zahnknirscher bzw. mit der Bedeutung „Auseinanderstehende Zähne“.

claims.statement: Since the goats' personal names appear only in Snorri, they are presumably his invention; Gylfaginning chapter 21 reads: 'Thor has two goats called Tanngnióstr and Tanngrisnir.'
claims.statement_id: Karena nama-nama pribadi kedua kambing hanya muncul pada Snorri, diduga nama itu ciptaannya; Gylfaginning bab 21 berbunyi: "Thor memiliki dua kambing jantan, Tanngnióstr dan Tanngrisnir."
claims.quote: Da die persönlichen Namen nur bei Snorri erscheinen, ist davon auszugehen, dass sie seine Erfindung sind. „Þórr á hafra ii er svá heita: Tanngnióstr ok Tanngrisnir ...“

claims.statement: Loki and Thor stop at a peasant farmer's home for the night; Thor slaughters his goats, skins them and puts them in a pot.
claims.statement_id: Loki dan Thor singgah di rumah seorang petani dan menginap semalam; Thor menyembelih kambing-kambingnya, menguliti, dan memasukkannya ke dalam periuk.
claims.quote: Loki and Thor stop at the home of a peasant farmer, and there they are given lodging for a night. Thor slaughters his goats, skins them and puts them in a pot.

claims.statement: The peasant's son Þjálfi takes a goat ham-bone and splits it with a knife to reach the marrow.
claims.statement_id: Anak petani, Þjálfi, mengambil salah satu tulang paha kambing dan membelahnya dengan pisau untuk mengambil sumsumnya.
claims.quote: The peasant's son Þjálfi takes one of the goat ham-bones and uses a knife to split it open, breaking the bone to get to the marrow.

claims.statement: Thor raises his hammer Mjöllnir and blesses the goatskins; the goats stand up revived, but one of the two is lame in the hind leg.
claims.statement_id: Thor mengangkat palunya Mjöllnir dan memberkati kulit kambing; kambing-kambing itu bangkit, tetapi salah satunya pincang di kaki belakang.
claims.quote: Thor takes his hammer Mjöllnir, raises it, and blesses the goat skins. Resurrected, the goats stand, but one of the two goats is lame in the hind leg.

claims.statement: Beowulf rules wisely for fifty years until a slave wakes and angers a dragon by stealing a jewelled cup from its lair; the dragon burns the Geats' homes and lands, Beowulf resolves to fight it himself, and when it wounds him fatally, Wiglaf strikes with his sword and Beowulf kills it with his dagger.
claims.statement_id: Beowulf memerintah dengan bijak selama lima puluh tahun sampai seorang budak membangunkan dan membuat murka seekor naga dengan mencuri piala berpermata dari sarangnya; naga itu membakar rumah dan tanah kaum Geat, Beowulf memutuskan melawannya sendiri, dan ketika naga melukainya secara fatal, Wiglaf menyerang dengan pedang dan Beowulf membunuhnya dengan belati.
claims.quote: rules wisely for fifty years until a slave awakens and angers a dragon by stealing a jeweled cup from its lair. When the angry dragon mercilessly burns the Geats' homes (including Beowulf's) and lands, Beowulf decides to fight and kill the monster personally. ... When the dragon wounds Beowulf fatally, Wiglaf attacks it with his sword, and Beowulf kills it with his dagger.

claims.statement: Beowulf is the first English work to present a dragonslayer; though its dragon shows many common Germanic motifs, the poet was the first to combine them into a distinctive fire-breathing dragon, which was adapted for Middle-earth in J. R. R. Tolkien's The Hobbit (1937).
claims.statement_id: Beowulf adalah karya sastra Inggris pertama yang menampilkan pembunuh naga; walau naganya memuat banyak motif umum tradisi Jermanik, penyair Beowulf yang pertama memadukannya menjadi naga penyembur api yang khas, dan naga ini diadaptasi untuk Dunia Tengah dalam The Hobbit (1937) karya J. R. R. Tolkien.
claims.quote: Beowulf is the first piece of English literature to present a dragonslayer. Although the Beowulf dragon exhibits many existing motifs common to Germanic tradition, the Beowulf poet was the first to combine features and present a distinctive fire-breathing dragon. The Beowulf dragon was adapted for Middle-earth in J. R. R. Tolkien's The Hobbit (1937)

claims.statement: The dragonslayer legend already existed in Norse sagas such as the tale of Sigurd and Fáfnir, and the Beowulf poet incorporates common dragonlore motifs.
claims.statement_id: Legenda pembunuh naga sudah ada dalam saga Nordik seperti kisah Sigurd dan Fáfnir, dan penyair Beowulf memasukkan motif serta tema umum kisah naga ke dalam puisinya.
claims.quote: The legend of the dragonslayer already existed in Norse sagas such as the tale of Sigurd and Fáfnir, and the Beowulf poet incorporates motifs and themes common to dragonlore in the poem.

claims.statement: The fight symbolises Beowulf's stand against evil and destruction; the dragon acts as a mock 'goldking', treating an attack on Beowulf's kingdom as fit retribution for the theft of a single cup.
claims.statement_id: Pertarungan dengan naga melambangkan perlawanan Beowulf terhadap kejahatan dan kehancuran; naga itu sendiri bertindak sebagai "raja emas" tiruan yang menganggap serangan terhadap kerajaan Beowulf sebagai balasan pantas atas pencurian satu piala.
claims.quote: The fight with the dragon symbolizes Beowulf's stand against evil and destruction, and, as the hero, he knows that failure will bring destruction to his people after many years of peace. The dragon itself acts as a mock "goldking"; one who sees attacking Beowulf's kingdom as suitable retribution for the theft of just a single cup.

claims.statement: The dragon (Old English draca or wyrm) is the third and last foe of Beowulf in the Anglo-Saxon epic, one of the earliest European literary dragons: an evil reptile able to fly and crawl, breathing fire, with a poisonous bite.
claims.statement_id: Naga (draca atau wyrm dalam bahasa Inggris Kuno) adalah lawan ketiga dan terakhir Beowulf dalam epos Anglo-Saxon itu, salah satu contoh awal naga Eropa dalam sastra: reptil jahat yang bisa terbang dan merayap, menyembur api, dan gigitannya berbisa.
claims.quote: Un dragon (draca ou wyrm en vieil anglais) est le troisième et dernier adversaire du héros Beowulf dans le poème épique anglo-saxon Beowulf. C'est l'un des premiers exemples connus de dragon européen dans la littérature. Il en possède toutes les caractéristiques : c'est un reptile maléfique, capable de voler et de ramper, qui crache du feu et dont la morsure est empoisonnée.

claims.statement: The theft enraged the dragon, which had slept on the treasure for three hundred years, and it left its lair to wreak destruction on the Geats' kingdom in revenge.
claims.statement_id: Pencurian itu membuat murka naga yang telah tidur di atas harta itu selama tiga ratus tahun, dan ia keluar dari sarangnya untuk menebar kehancuran di kerajaan Geat sebagai balasan.
claims.quote: Ce vol enrage le dragon qui dormait sur le trésor depuis trois cents ans, et il quitte son repaire pour semer la destruction dans le royaume des Geats en représailles.

claims.statement: The trow or drow (also trowe or dtrow) is a malign or mischievous fairy or spirit in Orkney and Shetland folk tradition; sometimes seen as monstrous giants, sometimes as short fairies dressed in grey.
claims.statement_id: Trow atau drow (juga trowe atau dtrow) adalah peri atau roh jahat atau jahil dalam tradisi cerita rakyat kepulauan Orkney dan Shetland; kadang dipandang raksasa mengerikan, kadang sebaliknya peri pendek berpakaian kelabu.
claims.quote: or drow (also trowe, or dtrow) is a malignant or mischievous fairy or spirit in the folkloric traditions of the Orkney and Shetland islands. Trows may be regarded as monstrous giants at times, or quite the opposite, short-statured fairies dressed in grey.

claims.statement: Trows are nocturnal, like the Scandinavian troll; they leave their 'trowie knowes' (earthen mound dwellings) only in the evening, often enter houses as people sleep, love music, and in folktales kidnap or lure musicians to their dens.
claims.statement_id: Trow adalah makhluk malam seperti troll legenda Skandinavia; mereka keluar dari "trowie knowes" (gundukan tanah tempat tinggal) hanya di malam hari, sering masuk rumah saat penghuni tidur, menyukai musik, dan menurut kisah rakyat menculik atau memikat pemusik ke sarang mereka.
claims.quote: Trows are nocturnal creatures, like the troll of Scandinavian legend with which the trow shares many similarities. They venture out of their 'trowie knowes' (earthen mound dwellings) solely in the evening, and often enter households as the inhabitants sleep. Trows traditionally have a fondness for music, and folktales tell of their habit of kidnapping musicians or luring them to their dens.

claims.statement: Insular Scots trow and drow are inherited from Norn, the Old Norse dialect of the Northern Isles; drow derives from an unrecorded Norn *drau, from Old Norse draugr, an old word for revenant, devil or troll.
claims.statement_id: Kata trow dan drow dalam bahasa Scots kepulauan diwarisi dari Norn, dialek Nordik Kuno di Kepulauan Utara; bentuk drow berasal dari Norn *drau yang tak tercatat, dari Nordik Kuno draugr, kata lama untuk mayat hidup, setan, atau troll.
claims.quote: Insular Scots trow and drow are inherited words from Norn, the Old Norse dialect spoken in the Northern Isles before being driven out by Scots. The form drow derives from an unrecorded Norn: *drau (or thereof), from Old Norse: draugr , an old word for revenant, devil, troll, and thereof.

claims.statement: The form trow is thought to come from troll with a vocalised L, then merged with drow; in Scots the trow is defined as a mischievous 'sprite or fairy'.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk trow diduga berasal dari kata troll yang bunyi L-nya menjadi vokal, lalu bercampur dengan drow; dalam bahasa Scots, trow didefinisikan sebagai "roh atau peri" yang jahil.
claims.quote: The form trow is thought to stem from L-vocalization of troll ("troll"), and then intermixing with drow via linguistic and figurative convergence. ... The trow [trʌu] , in the Scots language, is defined as a "sprite or fairy" of mischievous nature

claims.statement: The trow or drow is a supernatural creature of the beliefs and folklore of Orkney and Shetland, north of Scotland, often compared with fairies and perhaps derived from selkies or the Norse troll.
claims.statement_id: Trow atau drow adalah makhluk gaib dari kepercayaan dan cerita rakyat kepulauan Orkney dan Shetland di utara Skotlandia, sering dibandingkan dengan peri dan mungkin berasal dari selkie atau troll Nordik.
claims.quote: Un trow ou drow est une créature surnaturelle issue des croyances et du folklore des îles Orcades et Shetland, au nord de l'Écosse. Les trows sont souvent comparées aux fées (faeries) et ils dérivent peut-être des selkies ou bien du troll nordique.

claims.statement: It was considered taboo to speak about trows, and unlucky to catch sight of one, though auspicious to hear one speaking.
claims.statement_id: Berbicara tentang trow dianggap tabu, dan melihat trow dianggap membawa sial, tetapi mendengar trow berbicara dianggap pertanda baik.
claims.quote: It was considered taboo to speak about trows. It was also considered unlucky to catch sight of a trow, though auspicious to hear one speaking.

claims.statement: Trows are of two kinds, hill-trows (land trows) and sea-trows, said to be mortal enemies.
claims.statement_id: Trow terdiri atas dua jenis, trow bukit (trow darat) dan trow laut, dan keduanya konon musuh bebuyutan.
claims.quote: Trows consist of two kinds, the hill-trows (land trows) and sea-trows, and the two kinds are said to be mortal enemies.

claims.statement: Hill-dwelling trows are said to be able to leave their dwellings ("knowes", knolls) only after sunset; if they miss the chance to return before sunrise they do not perish but must wait above ground.
claims.statement_id: Trow bukit dikatakan hanya dapat keluar dari tempat tinggal mereka ("knowe", bukit kecil) setelah matahari terbenam; bila terlambat kembali sebelum matahari terbit, mereka tidak mati tetapi harus menunggu di atas tanah.
claims.quote: Of the hill-dwelling types, it is said they can only appear out of their dwellings ("knowes"=knolls; "trowie knowes") after sunset, and if they miss the opportunity to return before sunrise, they do not perish but must await above ground

claims.statement: The stone circle on Fetlar is called the Haltadans ('Limping Dance') because, according to legend, the stones are music-loving trows petrified after dancing so absorbedly to the trowie fiddler's tunes that they failed to hide before dawn.
claims.statement_id: Lingkaran batu di Fetlar dijuluki Haltadans ('Tarian Pincang') karena menurut legenda batu-batu itu adalah sekelompok trow pencinta musik yang membatu setelah terlalu asyik menari mengikuti nada pemain biola trow sehingga gagal bersembunyi sebelum fajar.
claims.quote: The stone circle on Fetlar has been dubbed the Haltadans (meaning 'Limping Dance') since according to legend, they represent a group of petrified music-loving trows who were so engrossed by dancing to the trowie fiddler's tunes that they failed to hide before dawn's break.

claims.statement: Tales tell of human fiddlers abducted by trows to their mounds; though released after what seems a brief stay, many years have passed outside and the victim turns to dust or chooses to die.
claims.statement_id: Ada pula kisah pemain biola manusia yang diculik trow ke gundukan mereka; meski dilepas setelah tampaknya sebentar, bertahun-tahun telah berlalu di dunia luar dan korban menjadi debu atau memilih mati.
claims.quote: Tales are also told of human fiddlers being abducted by trows to their mounds, and although released after what seems a brief stay, many long years have elapsed in the outside world, and the victim turns to dust, or chooses to die.

claims.statement: According to this dictionary, trows were called hill-, land- or sea-trows according to their supposed haunts or abode.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus ini, trow disebut trow bukit, darat, atau laut sesuai dengan tempat yang dianggap sebagai tempat tinggal atau sarangnya.
claims.quote: They were called hill-, land-, or sea-trows acc. to their supposed haunts or abode.

claims.statement: A passage quoted in the dictionary describes sea-trows as great rolling creatures tumbling in the water which, if they come among fishermen's nets, break them and sometimes take them away.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kutipan dalam kamus menggambarkan trow laut sebagai makhluk besar yang berguling-guling di air; bila masuk ke jaring nelayan, mereka merobeknya dan kadang membawanya pergi.
claims.quote: Sea-Trowes, great rolling Creatures, tumbling in the Waters, which if they come among their nets, they break them, and sometimes takes them away with them.

claims.statement: A passage quoted in the dictionary says that when a cow or sheep falls sick or dies, it is firmly believed the real animal was taken away and something of trowie breed put in its place.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kutipan dalam kamus menyebut bahwa bila sapi atau domba jatuh sakit atau mati, orang sangat percaya hewan aslinya telah dibawa pergi dan digantikan sesuatu dari jenis trow.
claims.quote: When a cow or sheep happens to turn sick or die, it is firmly believed that the real animal has been taken away and something of a trowie breed substituted in its place.

claims.statement: A passage quoted in the dictionary says newly confined women had to be watched lest they be carried off to act as wet-nurse to a trowling.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kutipan dalam kamus menyebut perempuan yang baru melahirkan harus dijaga agar tidak dibawa pergi untuk menjadi pengasuh susu bagi seorang trowling.
claims.quote: Females newly confined must be watched lest they be carried off to perform the office of wet-nurse to some trowling.

claims.statement: A passage quoted in the dictionary says that in autumn, at Hallowmass, folk had seen the peerie folk, or trows, coming forth on their nightly travels.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kutipan dalam kamus menyebut orang pernah melihat "peerie folk", atau trow, keluar dalam perjalanan malam mereka pada musim gugur, di Hallowmass.
claims.quote: In the autumn, at Hallowmass, folk had seen the ferry-kairds being parted, and the peerie folk, or trows, coming forth on their nightly travels.

claims.statement: A passage quoted in the dictionary states that the trows do not differ from the fairies of the Lowlands, or the Sighean of the Highlanders.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kutipan dalam kamus menyatakan bahwa trow tidak berbeda dari peri dataran rendah, atau Sighean orang Highlands.
claims.quote: The trows do not differ from the fairies of the Lowlands, or Sighean of the Highlanders.

claims.statement: The dictionary defines "trowie knowe" as a knoll inhabited by trolls, a fairy hill.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus, "trowie knowe" adalah bukit kecil yang dihuni troll, bukit peri.
claims.quote: (8) trowie knowe, a knoll inhabited by trolls, a fairy hill

claims.statement: The dictionary's etymology note says the earliest recorded form, troll, in 1503, may be a scribal representation of trow.
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan etimologi kamus, bentuk tercatat paling awal, troll, pada 1503, mungkin penulisan juru tulis untuk trow.
claims.quote: The earliest form recorded, troll, in 1503, may be a scribal representation of trow.

claims.statement: The Bøyg (Norwegian Bøygen), also called the 'Great Bøyg of Etnedal', is a legendary creature of Scandinavian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Bøyg (Norwegia: Bøygen), juga disebut "Bøyg Besar dari Etnedal", adalah makhluk legenda dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia.
claims.quote: also referred to as the "Great Bøyg of Etnedal" is a legendary gnome-like creature in Scandinavian folklore.

claims.statement: It is a great troll from Telemark and Gudbrandsdalen, usually a giant slimy serpent blocking travellers; the name means 'bend', 'twist' or 'curve', and it appears in the tale of Per Gynt, basis of Henrik Ibsen's play Peer Gynt.
claims.statement_id: Bøyg adalah troll besar dari Telemark dan Gudbrandsdalen, biasanya digambarkan sebagai ular raksasa berlendir yang menghalangi pengembara; namanya berarti "tikungan", "pilinan", atau "lengkungan", dan ia muncul dalam dongeng Per Gynt yang menjadi dasar drama Peer Gynt karya Henrik Ibsen.
claims.quote: It is a great troll from Telemark and Gudbrandsdalen. It is commonly characterized as a giant, slimy serpent which stands as a hindrance to travellers. The name means 'bend', 'twist' or 'curve'. It appears in the fairy-tale of Per Gynt, the basis for Henrik Ibsen's play Peer Gynt.

claims.statement: Bøyg, often called Bøygen ('the bent one'), is a supernatural being or troll in the form of a giant serpent in Norwegian folk belief; it can be invisible, tries to block and spoil people's ways, and is best known today from Henrik Ibsen's 1867 play Peer Gynt.
claims.statement_id: Bøyg, sering disebut Bøygen ("yang membungkuk"), adalah makhluk gaib atau troll berwujud ular raksasa dalam kepercayaan rakyat Norwegia; ia bisa juga tak terlihat, berusaha menghalangi dan merusak urusan orang, dan kini paling dikenal dari drama Peer Gynt (1867) karya Henrik Ibsen.
claims.quote: Bøyg, ofte omtalt i bestemt form Bøygen, det vil si «den som er bøyd», er et overnaturlig vesen eller troll som opptrer i form av en kjempeslange i norsk folketro. Skikkelsen, som også kan være usynlig, prøver å stille seg i veien og ødelegge for folk. I dag er figuren mest kjent fra Henrik Ibsens skuespill Peer Gynt fra 1867.

claims.statement: Bøygen may be a troll or giant serpent known from legends and tales of Telemark and Gudbrandsdalen, including Asbjørnsen's stories of the great hunter Per Gynt; similar stories are known from Denmark and Sweden.
claims.statement_id: Bøygen bisa berupa troll atau ular raksasa yang dikenal dari legenda dan dongeng Telemark dan Gudbrandsdalen, antara lain dari kisah Asbjørnsen tentang pemburu ulung Per Gynt; kisah serupa juga dikenal dari Denmark dan Swedia.
claims.quote: Bøygen kan være et troll eller en kjempeslange kjent fra sagn og eventyr fra Telemark og Gudbrandsdalen, blant annet fra Asbjørnsens historier om storskytteren Per Gynt. Liknende historier er også kjent fra Danmark og Sverige.

claims.statement: Old Norse baugr meant 'ring' or 'curve' but could also be a kenning for 'serpent'; bøyg and Bøygen are used figuratively for a large, vague obstacle or problem.
claims.statement_id: Kata Nordik Kuno baugr berarti "cincin" atau "lengkungan" dan bisa juga dipakai sebagai kiasan untuk "ular"; kata bøyg dan Bøygen secara kiasan dipakai untuk hambatan yang besar dan tak jelas, atau masalah.
claims.quote: Det norrøne ordet baugr betød «ring» eller «krumning», men kunne også brukes som en omskrivning for «orm». Ordene bøyg og Bøygen kan i overført betydning også brukes om en forhindring, gjerne stor og ubestemmelig, eller et problem.

claims.statement: In the tale, someone in the dark suddenly ran against something that, when he put out his hand, felt cold, slippery and big.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng itu, seseorang di kegelapan tiba-tiba menabrak sesuatu yang, saat disentuh dengan tangan, terasa dingin, licin, dan besar.
claims.quote: All of a sudden he ran against something, and when he put his hand out he felt it was cold and slippery and big.

claims.statement: Peer realised he was walking in a ring because the Boyg had curled itself round the sæter; the Boyg then shifted a little so that Peer got past.
claims.statement_id: Peer sadar bahwa ia berjalan berputar karena Boyg telah melingkarkan dirinya mengelilingi sæter; Boyg kemudian bergeser sedikit sehingga Peer dapat lewat.
claims.quote: he understood that he was walking in a ring, and that the Boyg had curled itself round the sæter. Thereupon it shifted a little, so that Peer got past.

claims.statement: Asked what it was, the Boyg answered that it was the big Boyg from Etnedale, the Troll-Monster. Peer's three shots into its head did not harm it: the Boyg told him to fire another, but the next bullet would have rebounded against Peer himself.
claims.statement_id: Ketika ditanya siapa dirinya, Boyg menjawab bahwa ia Boyg besar dari Etnedale, sang Troll-Monster. Tiga tembakan Peer ke kepalanya tidak melukainya: Boyg menyuruhnya menembak lagi, tetapi peluru berikutnya akan memantul mengenai Peer sendiri.
claims.quote: “What are you?” asked Peer. “Oh, I am the big Boyg from Etnedale,” said the Troll-Monster. Peer did not lose a moment, but fired three shots right into its head. “Fire another,” said the Boyg. But Peer knew better; if he had fired another shot, the bullet would have rebounded against himself.

claims.statement: Wherever Peer put out his hands or tried to get past, he felt the Boyg encircling him.
claims.statement_id: Ke mana pun Peer mengulurkan tangan atau mencoba lewat, ia merasakan Boyg melingkarinya.
claims.quote: “Oh, it’s the great Boyg,” was the answer. Where-ever he put his hands out or tried to get past, he felt the Boyg encircling him.

claims.statement: The translators' footnote says the root idea of the name seems to be bending and sinuousness, comparing Norwegian böie and German biegen, "to bend".
claims.statement_id: Catatan penerjemah menyebut gagasan dasar nama itu tampaknya membungkuk dan berkelok-kelok, dibandingkan dengan kata Norwegia böie dan kata Jerman biegen, "membengkokkan".
claims.quote: The root-idea seems to be that of bending, of sinuousness; compare Norwegian böie, German biegen, to bend.

claims.statement: According to the translators, as far as they know the name occurs in no folk-tale other than that of Peer Gynt.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penerjemah, sejauh mereka ketahui nama itu tidak muncul dalam dongeng rakyat lain selain dongeng Peer Gynt.
claims.quote: So far as we are aware, the name occurs in no other folk-tale save that of Peer Gynt.

claims.statement: In the introduction to the translation of Ibsen's play, the Boyg is called that vague, shapeless, ubiquitous, inevitable, invulnerable Thing Peer meets in Act II, Scene 7; Ibsen found it in the folk-tale.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pengantar terjemahan drama Ibsen, Boyg disebut sebagai Sesuatu yang samar, tak berbentuk, ada di mana-mana, tak terhindarkan, dan kebal yang ditemui Peer di Babak II Adegan 7; Ibsen menemukannya dalam dongeng rakyat.
claims.quote: Much more difficult is the interpretation of the Boyg ... that vague, shapeless, ubiquitous, inevitable, invulnerable Thing which Peer encounters in the following scene (Act II. Sc. 7). Ibsen found it in the folk-tale, and was attracted, no doubt, by the sheer uncanniness and eerieness of the idea.

claims.statement: In Ibsen's play Peer tells the Boyg to clear the way, but the voice answers "Go roundabout, Peer!" and Peer replies that he will go through.
claims.statement_id: Dalam drama Ibsen, Peer menyuruh Boyg minggir, tetapi suara itu menjawab "Pergilah memutar, Peer!" dan Peer menjawab bahwa ia akan menembus langsung.
claims.quote: Clear the way then, Boyg! THE VOICE. Go roundabout, Peer! PEER. No, through!

claims.statement: In Ibsen's play Peer gropes around and describes the Boyg as "not dead, not living; all slimy; misty; not so much as a shape".
claims.statement_id: Dalam drama Ibsen, Peer meraba-raba dan menggambarkan Boyg sebagai "tidak mati, tidak hidup; berlendir; berkabut; bahkan tanpa bentuk".
claims.quote: THE VOICE. The Boyg. PEER. ... Not dead, not living; all slimy; misty. Not so much as a shape!

claims.statement: In Ibsen's play the Boyg refuses to strike or fight and says that the great Boyg conquers but does not fight.
claims.statement_id: Dalam drama Ibsen, Boyg menolak memukul atau bertarung dan berkata bahwa Boyg besar menang tanpa bertarung.
claims.quote: The Boyg isn't mad. PEER. Strike! THE VOICE. The Boyg strikes not. PEER. Fight! You shall! THE VOICE. The great Boyg conquers, but does not fight.

claims.statement: At the end of the scene in Ibsen's play the Boyg shrinks to nothing and gasps that Peer was too strong and there were women behind him.
claims.statement_id: Di akhir adegan dalam drama Ibsen, Boyg menyusut menjadi tiada dan berkata terengah bahwa Peer terlalu kuat dan ada perempuan di belakangnya.
claims.quote: THE BOYG. ... Shrinks up to nothing, and says in a gasp ... He was too strong. There were women behind him.

claims.statement: The translators' note says the Peer Gynt story occurs in Asbjörnsen's "Reindeer-hunting in the Rondë Hills", published at Christiania in 1848, and is told by the peasant guides who accompany a shooting-party into the mountains.
claims.statement_id: Catatan penerjemah menyebut kisah Peer Gynt terdapat dalam "Reindeer-hunting in the Rondë Hills" karya Asbjörnsen, terbit di Christiania tahun 1848, dan dituturkan oleh pemandu petani yang menemani rombongan berburu ke pegunungan.
claims.quote: The stories of Peer Gynt and Gudbrand Glesnë both occur in Asbjörnsen’s “Reindeer-hunting in the Rondë Hills” ... Christiania, 1848). They are told by the peasant guides or gillies who accompany a shooting-party into the mountains

claims.statement: In German folklore the drude is a malevolent female nocturnal spirit of Germanic mythology, a sort of Alp or witch-hag tied to nightmares, prevalent in southern Germany, also called trude.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, drude adalah sejenis roh malam perempuan yang jahat dalam mitologi Jermanik, semacam Alp atau nenek sihir yang dikaitkan dengan mimpi buruk, terutama di Jerman selatan, dan juga disebut trude.
claims.quote: is a kind of malevolent female nocturnal spirit in Germanic mythology, a sort of alp or witch-hag associated with nightmares, prevalent especially in Southern Germany. It also occurs in the form or trude .

claims.statement: The word is attested as trute in late Middle High German, and in the 16th century trute also became a general term for 'witch'.
claims.statement_id: Kata ini tercatat sebagai trute dalam bahasa Jerman Hulu Pertengahan akhir, dan pada abad ke-16 trute juga dipakai sebagai sebutan umum untuk "penyihir".
claims.quote: The word is attested as trute in late Middle High German. ... The word trute also came to be used as a generic term for "witch" in the 16th century (Hans Sachs).

claims.statement: Middle High German trute relates to Old Norse troða ('to tread, trample') and German treten, the etymology deemed most plausible; in later Bavarian tradition the female Trude had male counterparts called Truder, Trudner or Truderer.
claims.statement_id: Kata Jerman Hulu Pertengahan trute berkaitan dengan Nordik Kuno troða ("menginjak, menginjak-injak") dan kata Jerman modern treten, etimologi yang dianggap paling masuk akal; dalam tradisi Bayern kemudian, Trude perempuan punya pasangan lelaki bernama Truder, Trudner, atau Truderer.
claims.quote: Middle High German trute is etymologically related to Old Norse troða ("to tread, to trample"), i.e., is related to modern German verb treten ("to tread, to step"); this is considered the most plausible etymology in modern philological opinion. ... In later Bavarian folklore tradition, the female Trude had male counterparts called Truder , Trudner , or Truderer

claims.statement: The drude is blamed for the Alpdruck nightmare ('elf pressure') and so counted a subtype of the Alp in attack; in some lore she is a witch who can be small or large, and only her spirit leaves the body to torment sleepers.
claims.statement_id: Drude dianggap penyebab mimpi buruk Alpdruck ("tekanan elf") sehingga dalam cara menyerang dipandang subtipe Alp; menurut sebagian cerita ia penyihir yang bisa berukuran kecil atau besar, dan konon hanya rohnya yang keluar dari tubuh untuk menyiksa orang yang tidur.
claims.quote: Drude is held responsible for causing the nightmare Alpdruck ("elf pressure"), thus considered just a subtype of an Alp, as far as its attack behavior is concerned. According to some folklore, the drude is a witch who can assume various sizes, small or large ... It is also said that only the witch's spirit drifts out of body to perform their handiwork tormenting people (in their sleep).

claims.statement: The Drude (also Drute, Trude, Trute; male Druder or Bavarian Truderer) is a folk-belief being that sits on sleepers' chests at night causing nightmares, oppression and breathlessness; in the Oldenburg area it is called Walrider or Walriderske.
claims.statement_id: Drude (juga Drute, Trude, Trute; lelaki Druder atau dalam bahasa Bayern Truderer) adalah makhluk kepercayaan rakyat yang pada malam hari duduk di dada orang tidur dan menimbulkan mimpi buruk, rasa tertekan, dan sesak napas; di Oldenburg ia disebut Walrider atau Walriderske.
claims.quote: Eine Drude (auch Drute, Trude, Trute, Trut, männlich Drud, Druder, Drudner, Trutner oder bairisch Truderer) ist ein Wesen des Volksglaubens, das sich nachts auf die Brust von Schlafenden setzt und Albträume, Beklemmungen und Atemnot verursacht. ... sowie im oldenburgischen Raum Walrider, Walriderske.

claims.statement: As drudes these pressing spirits are widespread in southern Germany and Austria: women condemned to find a victim each night, adults, children, animals, even trees and stones; their soul leaves the body, slips through cracks and keyholes and appears as a cat, straw or feather.
claims.statement_id: Di Jerman selatan dan Austria, drude adalah perempuan yang dikutuk mencari korban setiap malam, orang dewasa, anak, hewan, juga pohon dan batu; rohnya masuk lewat celah dan lubang kunci dan tampil dalam berbagai rupa seperti kucing, sedotan, atau bulu.
claims.quote: Hier sind Frauen, die dazu verdammt sind, sich jede Nacht ein Opfer zum Drücken suchen zu müssen: Erwachsene, Kinder und Haustiere werden heimgesucht, aber auch Bäume und Steine. ... kann als Geist durch kleinste Spalten und Schlüssellöcher in ein Zimmer dringen und dann in verschiedener Gestalt erscheinen (z. B. als Katze, Strohhalm oder Feder).

claims.statement: The magic sign Drudenfuß, also Drudenkreuz, is said to protect against them; by legend it comes from a drude's bird-like footprint.
claims.statement_id: Tanda gaib Drudenfuß, juga disebut Drudenkreuz, konon melindungi dari drude; menurut sage, tanda ini berasal dari jejak kaki drude yang mirip kaki burung.
claims.quote: Das Zauberzeichen Drudenfuß, auch Drudenkreuz genannt, soll gegen sie schützen. Der Ursprung dieses Zeichens liegt der Sage nach im vogelartigen Fußabdruck einer Drude.

claims.statement: Drudensteine (also Hühnergott), pebbles with a natural hole called the 'eye', were also believed to ward drudes off and were hung by a cord in the roof.
claims.statement_id: Drudenstein (juga Hühnergott), kerikil dengan lubang alami yang disebut "mata", juga dipercaya menangkal drude dan digantung dengan tali di rangka atap rumah.
claims.quote: Ebenfalls abwehrende Wirkung sollten Drudensteine (auch Hühnergott genannt) haben, die Kieselsteine mit einem natürlichen Loch, dem sogenannten Auge sind. Diese wurden zur Abwehr mit einem Band oder einer Schnur im Dachstuhl des Hauses aufgehängt.
