claims.statement: Ekke Nekkepenn (also Eke Nekepen) is a North Frisian legendary figure; in the mid-19th century the local researcher, folklorist and artist Christian Peter Hansen portrayed him as a merman living with his wife Rahn on the North Sea floor and playing tricks on seafarers and North Frisian islanders.
claims.statement_id: Ekke Nekkepenn (juga Eke Nekepen) adalah tokoh legenda Frisia Utara; pada pertengahan abad ke-19 peneliti lokal, ahli folklor, dan seniman grafis Christian Peter Hansen menggambarkannya sebagai lelaki laut yang tinggal bersama istrinya Rahn di dasar Laut Utara dan mengusili pelaut serta penduduk kepulauan Frisia Utara.
claims.quote: is a North Frisian legendary figure. In the middle of the 19th century, the local researcher, folklorist, and graphic artist Christian Peter Hansen ... portrayed Ekke Nekkepenn as a merman who lives with his wife Rahn at the bottom of the North Sea and plays mischievous tricks on seafarers and residents of the North Frisian Islands.

claims.statement: In Theodor Storm's novella Die Regentrude, published in 1866, a little fire-man called Eckeneckepenn appears who withers the fields with harmful magic.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel Theodor Storm Die Regentrude yang terbit 1866, muncul peri api kecil bernama Eckeneckepenn yang dengan sihir jahatnya membuat ladang layu.
claims.quote: In Theodor Storms 1866 veröffentlichter Novelle Die Regentrude taucht ein Feuermännlein mit dem Namen Eckeneckepenn auf, das mit seinem Schadenzauber für das Verdorren der Felder sorgt.

claims.statement: The tale begins with Ekke Nekkepenn asking the wife of the captain of a storm-tossed Sylt ship bound for England to help with his child's birth; she is led to his wife Rahn on the North Sea floor and, after a successful birth, returns to the surface richly gifted with gold and silver.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya bermula ketika Ekke Nekkepenn meminta istri kapten kapal Sylt yang diterjang badai menuju Inggris membantu persalinan anaknya; perempuan itu dibawa ke istrinya Rahn di dasar Laut Utara dan, setelah persalinan berhasil, kembali ke permukaan dengan hadiah emas dan perak.
claims.quote: Die Erzählung beginnt damit, dass Ekke Nekkepenn die Frau des Kapitäns eines im Sturm nach England laufenden Sylter Schiffes um Hilfe bei der Geburt seines Kindes bittet. Die schöne und hilfsbereite Kapitänsfrau wird vom Meermann zu seiner auf dem Grunde der Nordsee lebenden Frau Rahn geführt und kommt nach gelungener Geburt reichbeschenkt mit Gold und Silber an die Meeresoberfläche zurück.

claims.statement: Years later, with Rahn now 'old and wrinkly', Ekke Nekkepenn decides to take the captain's wife; seeing the Rantum captain's ship, he gets Rahn on the seabed to grind salt, and the strong vortex pulls the Sylt ship down.
claims.statement_id: Bertahun-tahun kemudian, karena Rahn telah "tua dan keriput", Ekke Nekkepenn ingin mengambil istri kapten itu; saat melihat kapal kapten dari Rantum, ia membujuk Rahn yang duduk di dasar laut untuk menggiling garam, dan pusaran kuat yang timbul menenggelamkan kapal Sylt itu.
claims.quote: Several years later, Ekke Nekkepenn remembered this incident and decides – now that Rahn has become "old and wrinkly" – to take the captain's wife as his own. When he sees the Rantumer Captain's ship one day, he persuades Rahn, who's sitting on the seabed, to grind salt, and the resulting powerful vortex pulls down the Sylt ship

claims.statement: Ekke fell in love with a young girl from Rantum who was forced to say yes; when she regretted it, he promised her freedom if by the next evening she could name him in full, and no one knew the name until she heard a song from the dunes by the beach.
claims.statement_id: Ekke jatuh cinta kepada gadis muda dari Rantum yang dipaksa menerimanya; ketika gadis itu menyesal, Ekke berjanji membebaskannya bila sebelum malam berikutnya ia dapat menyebut nama lengkapnya, dan tak seorang pun tahu nama itu sampai ia mendengar nyanyian dari bukit pasir di pantai.
claims.quote: Ekke blev forelsket i en ung pige fra Rantum, som blev tvunget til at give ham jaordet. Senere fortrød hun sit ja. Ekke lovede hende omsider, at hvis hun indenfor den næste aften kunne nævne ham ved hans fulde navn, så skulle hun få sin frihed igen. Men ingen kendte navnet, indtil hun ved stranden hørte en sang, der lød ud fra klitterne:

claims.statement: Ekke Nekkepenn (Föhr Frisian Eke Nekepen) is a North Frisian legendary figure who by legend lives with his wife Ran on the North Sea floor teasing seafarers and islanders; he corresponds in many ways to Ægir, and the material was also worked into Theodor Storm's novella Die Regentrude of 1863.
claims.statement_id: Ekke Nekkepenn (Frisia Föhr: Eke Nekepen) adalah tokoh legenda Frisia Utara yang menurut sage tinggal bersama istrinya Ran di dasar Laut Utara dan mengusili pelaut serta penduduk pulau; dalam banyak hal ia padanan Ægir, dan kisahnya juga diolah dalam novel Theodor Storm Die Regentrude dari 1863.
claims.quote: Ekke Nekkepenn (på førfrisisk Eke Nekepen) er en nordfrisisk sagnfigur. Ifølge sagnet lever figuren sammen med sin kone Ran på bunden af Vesterhavet og driller søfarere og beboerne på de nordfrisiske øer. Han modsvarer på mange punkter Ægir. ... Stoffet blev også indarbejdet i Theodor Storms novelle Die Regentrude fra 1863.

claims.statement: In European folklore and myth the Erlking is a sinister elf lingering in the woods, stalking children who stay too long and killing them with a single touch.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat dan mitos Eropa, Erlking adalah elf jahat yang berdiam di hutan, mengintai anak-anak yang terlalu lama di hutan, dan membunuh mereka dengan sekali sentuh.
claims.quote: In European folklore and myth, the Erlking is a sinister elf who lingers in the woods. He stalks children who stay in the woods for too long and kills them with a single touch.

claims.statement: The name Erlking (Erlkönig, 'alder-king') was used in German Romanticism for a spirit or 'king of the fairies' and is usually thought to derive from Danish folklore's ellekonge (older elverkonge, 'elf-king').
claims.statement_id: Nama Erlking (Erlkönig, "raja pohon alder") dipakai dalam Romantisisme Jerman untuk roh atau "raja para peri" dan umumnya dianggap turunan dari ellekonge (lebih tua: elverkonge, "raja elf") dalam cerita rakyat Denmark.
claims.quote: is a name used in German Romanticism for the figure of a spirit or "king of the fairies". It is usually assumed that the name is a derivation from the ellekonge (older elverkonge, i.e. "Elf-king") in Danish folklore.

claims.statement: The name was first used by Johann Gottfried Herder in Erlkönigs Tochter (1778), adapted from the Danish ballad Hr. Oluf han rider (1739), then taken up by Goethe in Erlkönig (1782), set by Schubert and others; Goethe added a new sense, 'Erl' meaning 'black alder', not 'elf'.
claims.statement_id: Nama ini pertama dipakai Johann Gottfried Herder dalam balada Erlkönigs Tochter (1778), saduran balada rakyat Denmark Hr. Oluf han rider (1739), lalu diambil Goethe dalam puisi Erlkönig (1782) yang digubah Schubert dan lainnya; Goethe menambah makna baru karena "Erl" berarti "alder hitam", bukan "elf".
claims.quote: The name was first used by Johann Gottfried Herder in his ballad Erlkönigs Tochter (1778), an adaptation of the Danish folk ballad Hr. Oluf han rider (1739), and was taken up by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe in his poem Erlkönig (1782), which was set to music by Schubert and others. Goethe added a new meaning, as "Erl" means not "elf" but "black alder"

claims.statement: According to the early linguist Jacob Grimm, the term comes from the Scandinavian word ellekonge, Danish for 'king of the elves'.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ahli bahasa awal Jacob Grimm, istilah ini berasal dari kata Skandinavia ellekonge, bahasa Denmark untuk "raja para elf".
claims.quote: According to the early linguist Jacob Grimm, the term originates with a Scandinavian word, ellekonge, Danish for "king of the elves"

claims.statement: The Erlkönig (Roi des Aulnes) is an imaginary figure in several German poems and ballads, an evil creature haunting the forests and leading travellers to their death.
claims.statement_id: Erlkönig (Roi des Aulnes) adalah tokoh khayalan dalam sejumlah puisi dan balada Jerman yang digambarkan sebagai makhluk jahat penghantu hutan yang menyeret para pengembara menuju kematian.
claims.quote: L'Erlkönig (Roi des Aulnes) est un personnage imaginaire représenté dans un certain nombre de poèmes et ballades allemands comme une créature maléfique qui hante les forêts et entraîne les voyageurs vers leur mort.

claims.statement: In Herder's telling Sir Oluf rides to his wedding but is drawn by elfin music; the Ellerkonge's daughter invites him to dance, he refuses her and her gifts of gold, the furious elf strikes him down, and next morning his bride finds him dead.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Herder, Sir Oluf berkuda menuju pernikahannya tetapi terpikat musik para elf; putri Ellerkonge mengajaknya menari, ia menolak ajakan serta hadiah emasnya, sang elf yang murka memukulnya jatuh, dan esok paginya pengantinnya menemukannya mati.
claims.quote: un homme du nom de Sir Oluf chevauchant pour son mariage mais attiré par la musique des elfes. Une elfe vierge, la fille du Ellerkonge, apparaît et l'invite à danser avec elle. Il refuse la proposition et son offre de cadeaux et d'or. Furieuse, elle le frappe et le fait tomber à terre. Le lendemain matin, le jour de son mariage, son épouse le trouve à cet endroit, mort

claims.statement: Other suggestions exist; in 1836 Halling proposed a link with the Turkic and Mongolian death god or psychopomp Erlik Khan.
claims.statement_id: Ada pula usulan lain; pada 1836 Halling mengaitkannya dengan dewa kematian atau penuntun arwah Turkik dan Mongol, Erlik Khan.
claims.quote: Alternative suggestions have also been made; in 1836, Halling suggested a connection with a Turkic and Mongolian god of death or psychopomp, known as Erlik Khan.

claims.statement: Fjalar is the name of several Norse mythological figures, meaning 'deceiver' or 'hider' (oszusta, ukrywającego); the most important is the dwarf (karzeł), brother of Galar, who with him killed Kvasir (Kvasera) and made the mead of poetry (miód poezji) from his blood.
claims.statement_id: Fjalar adalah nama beberapa tokoh mitologi Nordik yang berarti "penipu" atau "penyembunyi"; yang terpenting adalah kurcaci saudara Galar, yang bersama saudaranya membunuh Kvasir dan membuat madu puisi dari darahnya.
claims.quote: Fjalar – imię kilku postaci w mitologii nordyckiej, oznaczające „oszusta” lub „ukrywającego”. ... Kolejną, najważniejszą z postaci o tym imieniu, był karzeł, brat Galara. Razem z bratem zabili Kvasera, a z jego krwi stworzyli miód poezji.

claims.statement: Fjalar (Old Norse Fjalarr, from fela, 'to hide'; 'the Hider') is a dwarf in Norse mythology who, per Snorri's Edda, with his brother Galar killed the wise Kvasir; from his blood they made the mead of poetry, later stolen by the giant Suttung.
claims.statement_id: Fjalar (Nordik Kuno Fjalarr, dari fela, "menyembunyikan"; "si Penyembunyi") adalah nama kurcaci dalam mitologi Nordik yang menurut Edda Snorri bersama saudaranya Galar membunuh Kvasir yang bijak; dari darahnya mereka membuat madu puisi, yang kemudian dicuri raksasa Suttung.
claims.quote: Fjalar (gammelnorsk; Fjalarr av fela, «gjemme»; «Gjemmeren») på islansk; Fjalar «vitur» eller «fjölfròdur» som betyr klok. Fjalar er navn i norrøn mytologi på en dverg som ifølge Snorres Edda sammen med sin bror Galar drepte den vise Kvase. Av hans blod laget de skaldskapsmjøden. Skaldedrikken blir senere stjålet av jotnen Suttung.

claims.statement: The Völuspá lists Fjalar in its catalogue of dwarfs; the Hávamál speaks of Fjalar the Wise, whose ale gets the narrator (probably Odin) drunk, perhaps referring to the mead of poetry, in which case this Fjalar would be the mead-making dwarf.
claims.statement_id: Völuspá mencantumkan Fjalar dalam daftar kurcacinya; Hávamál menyebut Fjalar yang Bijak, yang birnya membuat sang penutur (mungkin Odin) mabuk, yang mungkin merujuk madu puisi, sehingga Fjalar itu bisa jadi sama dengan kurcaci pembuat madu.
claims.quote: Fjalara wymienia Völuspá w swoim katalogu karłów. Poemat Hávamál mówi o Fjalarze Mądrym, którego piwem upija się narrator (prawdopodobnie Odyn). Może to być odniesienie do miodu poezji, i w takim wypadku ten Fjalar byłby tożsamy z karłem, wytwórcą miodu.

claims.statement: In this translation of the Prose Edda, Kvasir was so wise that none could question him on anything he could not answer; when he came by invitation to the abode of the dwarves Fjalar and Galarr, they called him into private talk, killed him, and let his blood run into two vats and a kettle.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Prose Edda ini, Kvasir sangat bijak sehingga tak ada yang bisa menanyainya hal yang jawabannya tak ia ketahui; ketika ia datang atas undangan ke tempat kurcaci Fjalar dan Galarr, mereka memanggilnya untuk berbicara empat mata, membunuhnya, dan membiarkan darahnya mengalir ke dua bejana besar dan sebuah kuali.
claims.quote: This man is called Kvasir, and he was so wise that none could question him concerning anything but that he knew the solution. He went up and down the earth to give instruction to men; and when he came upon invitation to the abode of certain dwarves, Fjalar and Galarr, they called him into privy converse with them, and killed him, letting his blood run into two vats and a kettle.

claims.statement: The kettle is named Ódrerir and the vats Són and Bodn; they blended honey with the blood, producing a mead that makes whoever drinks it a skald or scholar.
claims.statement_id: Kuali itu bernama Ódrerir dan bejananya Són dan Bodn; mereka mencampur madu dengan darah itu sehingga jadilah madu yang membuat peminumnya menjadi skald atau cendekiawan.
claims.quote: The kettle is named Ódrerir, and the vats Són and Bodn; they blended honey with the blood, and the outcome was that mead by the virtue of which he who drinks becomes a skald or scholar.

claims.statement: The dwarves reported to the Æsir that Kvasir had choked on his own shrewdness, since no one there was wise enough to question his wisdom.
claims.statement_id: Para kurcaci melaporkan kepada bangsa Æsir bahwa Kvasir tersedak oleh kecerdikannya sendiri, sebab tak ada yang cukup bijak untuk menanyai hikmatnya.
claims.quote: The dwarves reported to the Æsir that Kvasir had choked on his own shrewdness, since there was none so wise there as to be able to question his wisdom.

claims.statement: The dwarves then invited the giant Gillingr and his wife, took Gillingr rowing at sea, rowed into the breakers and capsized the boat; Gillingr could not swim and perished.
claims.statement_id: Para kurcaci itu kemudian mengundang raksasa Gillingr dan istrinya, mengajak Gillingr berperahu di laut, lalu mendayung ke arah ombak pecah dan membalikkan perahu; Gillingr tak bisa berenang dan tewas.
claims.quote: Then these dwarves invited the giant who is called Gillingr to visit them, and his wife with him. Next the dwarves invited Gillingr to row upon the sea with them; but when they had gone out from the land, the dwarves rowed into the breakers and capsized the boat. Gillingr was unable to swim, and he perished

claims.statement: After the accident was reported to the dead man's wife, who wept aloud, Fjalar questioned her and then softly told his brother Galarr to go over the doorway and let a mill-stone fall on her head because her weeping wearied him; and Galarr did so.
claims.statement_id: Setelah kecelakaan itu dilaporkan kepada istri korban, yang menangis keras, Fjalar menanyainya lalu berbisik kepada saudaranya Galarr agar naik ke atas pintu dan menjatuhkan batu kilangan ke kepala perempuan itu karena tangisnya melelahkan, dan Galarr melakukannya.
claims.quote: They reported this accident to his wife, but she took it grievously and wept aloud. Then Fjalar asked her ... Then he spoke softly to Galarr his brother, bidding him go up over the doorway, when she should go out, and let a mill-stone fall on her head, saying that her weeping grew wearisome to him; and even so he did.

claims.statement: When the giant Suttungr, Gillingr's son, learned of this, he carried the dwarves out to sea and set them on a reef covered at high tide; they begged for their lives and offered him the precious mead as the price of reconciliation for his father's death.
claims.statement_id: Ketika raksasa Suttungr, putra Gillingr, mengetahui hal itu, ia membawa para kurcaci ke laut dan menempatkan mereka di karang yang tertutup air pasang; mereka memohon agar nyawa mereka diampuni dan sebagai tebusan menawarkan madu berharga itu atas kematian ayahnya.
claims.quote: Now when the giant Suttungr, Gillingr's son, learned of this, he went over and took the dwarves and carried them out to sea, and set them on a reef which was covered at high tide. They besought Suttungr to grant them respite of their lives, and as the price of reconciliation offered him the precious mead in satisfaction of his father's death.

claims.statement: In this translated poem, the speaker was dead-drunk when with Fjalar the wise, and drinking is best if one brings its wisdom home.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan puisi ini, penuturnya mabuk berat ketika bersama Fjalar yang bijak, dan minum paling baik bila orang membawa pulang hikmatnya.
claims.quote: Drunk I was, I was dead-drunk, When with Fjalar wise I was;'Tis the best of drinking if back one brings His wisdom with him home.

claims.statement: The translator's note says the Fjalar of that stanza is apparently another name for Suttung.
claims.statement_id: Catatan penerjemah menyebut Fjalar dalam bait itu tampaknya nama lain untuk Suttung.
claims.quote: Fjalar: apparently another name for Suttung. This stanza, and probably 13, seem to have been inserted as illustrative.

claims.statement: By local folklore, Gnome King Kyrië led the legendary kabouters of the Campine, North Brabant, the Netherlands; based in Hoogeloon, they travelled into neighbouring lands, and Kyrië lived on the Kerkakkers in the Kabouterberg ('gnome mountain') or Duivelsberg ('devil's mountain'), a tumulus.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat setempat, Raja Kurcaci Kyrië adalah pemimpin kabouter legendaris di wilayah Kempen, Brabant Utara, Belanda, para kabouter berpangkalan di desa Hoogeloon, dan Kyrië tinggal di Kerkakkers di Kabouterberg ("gunung kurcaci") atau Duivelsberg ("gunung setan"), sebuah tumulus.
claims.quote: is, according to local folklore, the leader of the legendary gnomes (kabouters) who lived in the Campine region of the province of North Brabant, the Netherlands. These gnomes had their base in the village of Hoogeloon. ... According to tradition the gnome king Kyrië lived on the Kerkakkers in the Kabouterberg ("gnome mountain"), also known as Duivelsberg ("devil's mountain"), a tumulus

claims.statement: The Campine gnomes were helpful beings aiding farmers and households in the Campine, the Peel and the Meierij; they came at night, did not want to be seen, and punished those who saw them, like a curious farmer blinded in one eye.
claims.statement_id: Kabouter Kempen adalah makhluk penolong yang terutama membantu petani dan rumah tangga di Kempen, Peel, dan Meierij; mereka datang di malam hari dan tak ingin dilihat, dan orang yang melihat mereka dihukum, seperti petani penasaran yang buta sebelah matanya.
claims.quote: The gnomes of the Campine were helpful creatures who helped mostly farmers and households in the Campine and also in the neighboring lands of the Peel and the Meierij. They came by night and did not want to be seen by people. If people did see them, they were punished by the gnomes. One story tells of an inquisitive farmer who spied on the gnomes and later became blind in one eye as a punishment.

claims.statement: Kyrië was shot by a hunter on the Riethoven heath, just reaching the Duivelsberg; the hunter heard the shocked gnomes say 'Kyrië is dead'; the king was buried in Hoogeloon, after which all the gnomes left for an unknown place.
claims.statement_id: Kyrië ditembak seorang pemburu di padang Riethoven, masih sempat mencapai Duivelsberg; pemburu itu mendengar kabouter yang terkejut berkata "Kyrië sudah mati"; sang raja dimakamkan di Hoogeloon, dan setelah itu semua kabouter pergi ke tempat yang tak diketahui.
claims.quote: Gnome king Kyrië was shot by a hunter in the heathlands of Riethoven. He had just enough strength to reach the Duivelsberg ... The hunter looked for what he had shot and heard the shocked gnomes say, "Kyrië is dead". ... Gnome king Kyrië was buried somewhere in Hoogeloon. After the death of their king, all the gnomes left for an unknown destination.

claims.statement: In one version the king's death is announced by a traveller, a narrative structure that may come from Plutarch.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu versi, kematian sang raja diumumkan seorang pengembara, struktur cerita yang mungkin berasal dari Plutarkhos.
claims.quote: In one version of the story, the king's death is announced by a traveler, a narrative structure that may come from Plutarch.

claims.statement: Kabouterkoning Kyrië is a figure in several legends and also a 1985 statue by Wim Gubbels on the Valensplein in Hoogeloon, which by the gnome tales is where the gnome king was buried.
claims.statement_id: Kabouterkoning Kyrië adalah tokoh dalam beberapa sage sekaligus nama patung karya Wim Gubbels tahun 1985 di Valensplein, Hoogeloon, yang menurut kisah kabouter juga tempat sang raja dimakamkan.
claims.quote: Kabouterkoning Kyrië is een personage dat in meerdere sagen voorkomt en is een gelijknamig standbeeld van Wim Gubbels uit 1985. Het standbeeld bevindt zich op het Valensplein midden in het centrum van de Nederlandse plaats Hoogeloon, wat tevens, volgens de kabouterverhalen, de plaats is waar de kabouterkoning zou zijn begraven.

claims.statement: On 9 April 2001 the statue was moved elsewhere on the same square because of the Valensplein's redesign, and at the same time a special 'Koning Kyrië Kruidenbitter' was introduced.
claims.statement_id: Pada 9 April 2001 patung itu dipindahkan ke tempat lain di alun-alun yang sama karena penataan ulang Valensplein, dan sekaligus diperkenalkan minuman khusus "Koning Kyrië Kruidenbitter".
claims.quote: Op 9 april 2001 werd dit beeld ten gevolge van de herinrichting van het Valensplein verplaatst naar een andere plek op hetzelfde plein. Tegelijkertijd werd ook het speciale 'Koning Kyrië Kruidenbitter' geïntroduceerd.

claims.statement: In the folk belief of the North Frisian islands of Sylt and Amrum, a ghost was called a gonger (from Wiedergänger).
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat di pulau-pulau Frisia Utara Sylt dan Amrum, gonger (dari Wiedergänger) adalah sebutan untuk hantu.
claims.quote: Als Gonger (von Wiedergänger) bezeichnete man im Volksglauben auf den nordfriesischen Inseln Sylt und Amrum ein Gespenst.

claims.statement: According to tales the 'innocently murdered' and those who moved boundary stones or ploughed away or ravaged land find no rest in the grave; blasphemers, suicides and self-cursers also return as gongers.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita, orang yang "dibunuh tanpa salah" serta orang yang memindahkan batu batas atau membajak dan merusak tanah tidak tenang di kubur; penghujat, orang bunuh diri, dan orang yang mengutuk dirinya juga kembali sebagai gonger.
claims.quote: Erzählungen zufolge finden „unschuldig Ermordete“ sowie Menschen, die Grundsteine versetzt oder Land abgepflügt bzw. verwüstet haben, keine Ruhe im Grab. Ebenso kehren Gotteslästerer, Selbstmörder und Personen, die sich selbst verflucht haben, als Gonger wieder.

claims.statement: When a sailor dies at sea he returns as a gonger to bring news of his death: at night he rises from the sea in the clothes he died in, visits his descendants' house, puts out the light, lies on a sleeper's blanket and leaves a trail of salt water.
claims.statement_id: Bila pelaut mati di laut, ia kembali sebagai gonger untuk membawa kabar kematiannya: malam hari ia keluar dari laut dengan pakaian saat mati, mendatangi rumah keturunannya, memadamkan lampu, berbaring di atas selimut orang yang tidur, dan meninggalkan jejak air asin.
claims.quote: Wenn ein Seemann auf dem Meer stirbt, kehrt er als Gonger zurück, um die Nachricht seines Todes zu überbringen. Dazu steigt er nachts in der Kleidung, die er zum Todeszeitpunkt getragen hat, aus dem Meer, und besucht das Haus seiner Nachkommen. Hier löscht er das Licht, legt sich auf die Decke eines Schlafenden und hinterlässt eine Spur aus Salzwasser.

claims.statement: On the North Frisian islands of Amrum and Sild (Sylt) gonger means a revenant (genganger); by folk belief gongers could be the innocently killed, suicides or blasphemers, and sailors who died at sea could return to haunt the island.
claims.statement_id: Di pulau-pulau Frisia Utara Amrum dan Sild (Sylt), gonger berarti arwah gentayangan; menurut kepercayaan rakyat, gonger bisa orang yang dibunuh tanpa salah, orang bunuh diri, atau penghujat, dan pelaut yang mati di laut juga bisa kembali ke pulau dan menghantui.
claims.quote: Gonger betegner på de nordfrisiske øer Amrum og Sild en genganger. Gongere kunne ifølge folketroen være uskyldigt dræbte, men også selvmordere eller gudsbespottere. Også sømænd, der døde på havet, kunne vende tilbage til øen og spøge.

claims.statement: Hugo Wolfgang Philipp used the belief in his 1930s play Der Gonger kommt; the TV film Gonger – Das Böse vergisst nie appeared in 2008, and the folk-rock band Versengold took it up in the song Die Gonger kommen.
claims.statement_id: Hugo Wolfgang Philipp mengolah kepercayaan ini dalam lakon Der Gonger kommt pada 1930-an; pada 2008 dibuat film televisi Gonger – Das Böse vergisst nie, dan band folk-rock Versengold mengangkatnya dalam lagu Die Gonger kommen.
claims.quote: Hugo Wolfgang Philipp verarbeitete in den 1930er Jahren den Glauben in seinem Theaterstück Der Gonger kommt. 2008 entstand der Fernsehfilm Gonger – Das Böse vergisst nie. Musikalisch verarbeitet wurde die Thematik von der Folk-Rock-Band Versengold in dem Lied Die Gonger kommen

claims.statement: In this folklore collection there are many Wiedergänger or Gongers: the innocently murdered, or those who moved boundary stones and ploughed away land, find no rest in the grave; blasphemers, those who cursed themselves, and suicides must also walk again.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kumpulan cerita rakyat ini, ada banyak Wiedergänger atau Gongers: orang yang dibunuh tanpa salah, atau yang memindahkan batu batas dan membajak tanah orang, tidak menemukan ketenangan di kubur; penghujat, orang yang mengutuk diri sendiri, dan pelaku bunuh diri juga harus berjalan kembali.
claims.quote: Es gibt da überhaupt manche Wiedergänger oder Gongers; denn wer unschuldig ermordet ist, oder Grundsteine versetzt und Land abgepflügt hat, findet keine Ruhe im Grabe. Ebenso müssen auch die Gotteslästerer und wer sich selbst verflucht und die Selbstmörder wiedergehen.

claims.statement: One must not give such a Gonger one's hand; it burns, turns black and falls off.
claims.statement_id: Seorang Gonger seperti itu tidak boleh diberi tangan; tangan itu terbakar, menjadi hitam, dan terlepas.
claims.quote: Einem solchen Gonger darf man nicht die Hand reichen; sie verbrennt, wird schwarz und fällt ab.

claims.statement: In Keitum on Sylt a woman once died before her confinement; she appeared several times to the preacher's servant and had no rest in the grave until scissors, needle and thread were laid in it, as is usually done for women in North Frisia.
claims.statement_id: Di Keitum, Sylt, seorang perempuan meninggal sebelum melahirkan; ia beberapa kali menampakkan diri kepada pelayan pendeta dan baru tenang di kubur setelah gunting, jarum, dan benang dimasukkan ke kuburnya; hal itu lazim dilakukan pada perempuan di Frisia Utara.
claims.quote: In Keitum auf Sylt starb einmal eine Frau vor ihrer Entbindung; da ist sie mehrere Male dem Knecht des Predigers erschienen und hat nicht eher Ruhe im Grabe gehabt, als bis man ihr Scheere, Nadel und Zwirn ins Grab gelegt. So tut man bei Frauen in Nordfriesland gewöhnlich.

claims.statement: When a relative has drowned at sea he afterwards reports it to his kin; whoever meets such a Gonger is not frightened but rather saddened.
claims.statement_id: Bila seorang kerabat tenggelam di laut, ia kemudian memberi kabar kepada sanak keluarganya; orang yang bertemu Gonger seperti itu tidak takut, melainkan bersedih.
claims.quote: Wenn einer von der Verwandtschaft auf der See ertrunken ist, meldet er es nachher den Anverwandten. Wem ein solcher Gonger begegnet, der erschrickt nicht, sondern wird vielmehr betrübt.

claims.statement: At dusk or at night he shows himself in the very clothes in which he drowned; he looks in at the front door leaning on it with his arms, walks about the house, soon vanishes and returns at the same time the next evening.
claims.statement_id: Pada senja atau malam ia menampakkan diri dengan pakaian yang ia kenakan saat tenggelam; ia menengok ke dalam dari pintu rumah dan bersandar dengan lengan di sana, berjalan di dalam rumah, lalu segera menghilang dan datang lagi pada waktu yang sama keesokan malamnya.
claims.quote: In der Abenddämmerung oder bei Nacht läßt er sich sehen in eben der Kleidung, worin er ertrunken ist. Er sieht dann zur Haustür herein und lehnt sich mit den Armen darauf, geht auch sonst im Hause herum, verschwindet aber bald und kommt am folgenden Abend um dieselbe Zeit wieder.

claims.statement: At night he opens the room door, usually in heavy pulled-up boots full of water, puts out the light with his hand and lies down on the sleeper's blanket; in the morning a little stream of salt water is found.
claims.statement_id: Pada malam hari ia membuka pintu kamar, biasanya dengan sepatu bot berat penuh air, memadamkan lampu dengan tangan, dan berbaring di atas selimut orang yang tidur; paginya orang menemukan aliran kecil air asin.
claims.quote: Nachts öffnet er, gewöhnlich in schweren aufgezogenen Stiefeln, die voll Wasser sind, die Stubentür, löscht mit der Hand das Licht aus und legt sich dem Schlafenden auf die Decke. Am Morgen findet man einen kleinen Strom salzigen Wassers

claims.statement: If the relatives are not yet persuaded by this sign, the Gonger keeps appearing until they believe it; the Gonger also gives other signs.
claims.statement_id: Bila para kerabat belum yakin oleh tanda itu, Gonger muncul lagi sampai mereka percaya; Gonger juga memberi tanda-tanda lain.
claims.quote: Lassen die Verwandten durch dieses Zeichen sich noch nicht überreden, so erscheint der Gonger so lange wieder, bis sie es glauben. Der Gonger gibt auch andre Zeichen.

claims.statement: The gulon looks like a mix of animals, usually dog-sized and dog-shaped with cat-like head, ears and claws, a thick shaggy brown coat and a fox-like tail.
claims.statement_id: Gulon tampak seperti campuran berbagai hewan, biasanya seukuran dan sebentuk anjing dengan kepala, telinga, dan cakar seperti kucing, berbulu cokelat tebal yang kusut dan berekor seperti rubah.
claims.quote: It resembles a hodgepodge of various animals, usually described as being the size and shape of a dog, with some cat-like features such as the head, ears, and claws. It also supposedly has a thick coat of shaggy brown fur and a tail resembling that of a fox.

claims.statement: The gulon is notorious as a symbol of gluttony for its strange eating: after a kill it gorges until swollen, squeezes between two trees to push the meat through its body, then returns and repeats.
claims.statement_id: Gulon terkenal sebagai lambang kerakusan karena kebiasaan makannya yang ganjil: setelah membunuh, ia makan sampai menggembung, lalu menjepit diri di antara dua pohon untuk mendorong daging melalui tubuhnya, kemudian kembali makan dan mengulanginya.
claims.quote: The Gulon is notorious as a symbol of gluttony because of the strange eating habits it is supposed to have. It will make a kill and then gorge itself until it is swollen and unable to eat more, at which point it will find two trees and squeeze itself in between them, pushing the meat through its own body before returning to the kill and repeating the process.

claims.statement: The jerff, modern spelling järv, is in Scandinavian legend a blend of animals resembling a dog with a cat's head and claws, a thick coat and a fox-like tail; in Germany it is Vielfraß and in English Gulon.
claims.statement_id: Jerff, dalam ejaan modern Järv, dalam legenda Skandinavia adalah campuran berbagai hewan yang mirip anjing dengan kepala dan cakar kucing, berbulu tebal dan berekor seperti rubah; di Jerman ia dikenal sebagai Vielfraß dan dalam bahasa Inggris Gulon.
claims.quote: En Jerff eller med modern stavning Järv, är inom skandinavisk legend en blandning av olika djur men som ska likna en hund, med huvud och klor av en katt. Den ska även ha en tjock päls och en svans liknande den på en räv. I Tyskland är varelsen känd som Vielfraß och på engelska heter det Gulon.

claims.statement: Legends of the jerff are an early mention of the järv (wolverine), then unknown in southern Sweden.
claims.statement_id: Legenda tentang jerff merupakan sebutan awal tentang järv (wolverine), yang dulu belum dikenal di Swedia selatan.
claims.quote: Legender om jerffen är ett tidigt omnämnande av den i södra Sverige då okända järven.

claims.statement: According to the Bell Library, the animal marked "gulo" in that map section is Latin for the glutton (Gulo gulo), a member of the marten or weasel family, a large animal living in the northern parts of Scandinavia.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Perpustakaan Bell, hewan bertanda "gulo" di bagian peta itu adalah bahasa Latin untuk glutton (Gulo gulo), anggota keluarga marten atau musang, hewan besar yang hidup di bagian utara Skandinavia.
claims.quote: In the lower right is an animal with the designation gulo, Latin for the glutton (Gulo gulo) which belongs to the marten or weasel family. This large animal lives in the northern parts of Scandinavia.

claims.statement: Olaus writes that in bulk it is like a large dog; its ears and face resemble a cat's, its feet have very sharp claws, it has a shaggy body with a long brownish coat and a fox's tail, shorter and draped with thick fur, so that excellent winter caps can be made from it.
claims.statement_id: Olaus menulis bahwa dalam ukuran ia mirip anjing besar; telinga dan wajahnya mirip kucing, kakinya bercakar sangat tajam, tubuhnya berbulu lebat cokelat panjang, dan ekornya seperti ekor rubah yang lebih pendek dan berbulu tebal sehingga bisa dibuat topi musim dingin yang bagus.
claims.quote: Olaus says "In its bulk it is similar to a large dog. Its ears and face resemble a cat’s, and its feet have very sharp claws. It has a shaggy body with a long brownish coat, and a fox’s tail, though shorter and draped with thick fur, so that excellent winter caps can be made from it."

claims.statement: According to the passage quoted from Magnus, when the glutton finds a carcass it eats so furiously that its torso swells like a drum; it then finds a narrow space between trees and squeezes through to discharge its bowels forcibly, and returns to the carcass to stuff itself again.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kutipan dari Magnus, ketika glutton menemukan bangkai ia makan dengan sangat rakus sehingga badannya membengkak seperti genderang; lalu ia mencari celah sempit di antara pepohonan dan menyelinap melaluinya untuk mengeluarkan isi perutnya dengan paksa, kemudian kembali ke bangkai dan makan lagi.
claims.quote: When the glutton finds a carcass, it eats so quickly that "its furious meal makes its torso swell like a drum. Afterwards it finds a narrow space between trees and squeezes itself through, in order to discharge its bowels forcibly" (Magnus 1998, III:888). This completed, it returns to the carcass and stuffs itself once more.

claims.statement: The Bell Library notes its nearest relative in North America is the wolverine, and quotes the view that Olaus Magnus probably pictured them on his map from direct experience.
claims.statement_id: Perpustakaan Bell menyebut kerabat terdekatnya di Amerika Utara adalah wolverine, dan mengutip pendapat bahwa Olaus Magnus kemungkinan menggambarkannya pada petanya berdasarkan pengalaman langsung.
claims.quote: Its nearest relative in North America is the wolverine. "It was probably from direct experience that Olaus Magnus pictured them on his map" (George, 1969, 116).

claims.statement: The resource named for the gulon is Historia de gentibus septentrionalibus by Olaus Magnus (The History of the Northern People, 1555 AD).
claims.statement_id: Sumber yang disebut untuk gulon adalah Historia de gentibus septentrionalibus karya Olaus Magnus (Sejarah Bangsa-Bangsa Utara, 1555 M).
claims.quote: Historia de gentibus septentrionalibus by Olaus Magnus. (The History of the Northern People, 1555 AD)

claims.statement: In Norse mythology Hábrók is, per Grímnismál and quoted by Snorri Sturluson in Gylfaginning, the 'best of hawks' in a list of names representing the best of things; nothing more is known of it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Hábrók menurut Grímnismál, dan dikutip Snorri Sturluson dalam Gylfaginning, adalah "elang alap terbaik" dalam daftar nama yang mewakili yang terbaik dari segala hal; selain itu tak ada yang diketahui tentang makhluk ini.
claims.quote: In Norse mythology, Hábrók is, according to Grímnismál, and quoted by Snorri Sturluson in Gylfaginning, as the "best of hawks" in a list containing various other names which represent the best of things. However, nothing more is known of this creature.

claims.statement: The name is translated 'High Pants', perhaps referring to the bird's long legs.
claims.statement_id: Namanya diterjemahkan "celana tinggi", yang mungkin merujuk kaki burung itu yang panjang.
claims.quote: The name is translated as "High Pants" which may refer to the bird's long legs.

claims.statement: The Grímnismál stanza: Yggdrasil best of trees, Skíðblaðnir of ships, Óðinn greatest of gods, Sleipnir best of steeds, Bifröst of bridges, Bragi of skalds, Hábrók of hawks (halcones), and Garm of hounds (sabuesos).
claims.statement_id: Bait Grímnismál: Yggdrasil terbaik di antara pohon, Skíðblaðnir di antara kapal, Óðinn terbesar di antara dewa, Sleipnir terbaik di antara kuda, Bifröst di antara jembatan, Bragi di antara skald, Hábrók di antara elang alap, dan Garm di antara anjing pemburu.
claims.quote: El mejor de los árboles | Yggdrasil debe ser, Skíðblaðnir el mejor de los barcos; De todos los dioses | es Óðinn el más grande, Y Sleipnir el mejor de los corceles; Bifröst de los puentes, | Bragi de los escaldos, Hábrók de los halcones, | y Garm de los sabuesos.

claims.statement: The name can also be translated 'long trousers' (pantalones largos), perhaps referring to the bird's long legs.
claims.statement_id: Namanya juga dapat diterjemahkan "celana panjang", yang mungkin merujuk kaki burung itu yang panjang.
claims.quote: El nombre se puede traducir como «pantalones largos» que puede referirse a las patas alargadas del pájaro.

claims.statement: In this translated poem, Hobrok is named as the best of hawks in a list with Yggdrasil as best of trees, Skithblathnir best of boats, Othin greatest of the gods, Sleipnir best of steeds, Bilrost of bridges, Bragi of skalds and Garm of hounds.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan puisi ini, Hobrok disebut sebagai yang terbaik di antara elang alap dalam daftar yang terdiri dari pohon terbaik Yggdrasil, kapal terbaik Skithblathnir, dewa terbesar Othin, kuda terbaik Sleipnir, jembatan Bilrost, skald Bragi, dan anjing Garm.
claims.quote: The best of trees must Yggdrasil be, Skithblathnir best of boats; Of all the gods is Othin the greatest, And Sleipnir the best of steeds; Bilrost of bridges, Bragi of skalds, Hobrok of hawks, and Garm of hounds.

claims.statement: The translator's note states that nothing further is known of Hobrok.
claims.statement_id: Catatan penerjemah menyatakan tidak ada hal lain yang diketahui tentang Hobrok.
claims.quote: Hobrok: nothing further is known of him.

claims.statement: In this translation of the Gylfaginning, Hábrók is named as foremost among hawks in a stanza cited as the words of the Æsir themselves, together with Yggdrasill, Skídbladnir, Odin, Sleipnir, Bifröst, Bragi and Garmr.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Gylfaginning ini, Hábrók disebut sebagai yang terbaik di antara elang alap dalam bait yang dikutip sebagai kata-kata para Æsir sendiri, bersama Yggdrasill, Skídbladnir, Odin, Sleipnir, Bifröst, Bragi, dan Garmr.
claims.quote: Odin is of great might. Many examples are found in proof of this, as is here said in the words of the Æsir themselves: Ash Yggdrasill's trunk of trees is foremost, And Skídbladnir of ships; Odin of Æsir, of all steeds Sleipnir, Bifröst of bridges, and Bragi of skalds; Hábrók of hawks, and of hounds Garmr.

claims.statement: In Norse mythology Hjúki (possibly 'the one returning to health') and Bil ('instant') are a brother and sister who follow the personified Moon, Máni, across the heavens; both are attested only in the Prose Edda written by Snorri Sturluson in the 13th century.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Hjúki (Nordik Kuno, mungkin berarti "yang kembali sehat") dan Bil ("sekejap") adalah sepasang kakak-adik yang mengikuti Bulan yang dipersonifikasikan, Máni, di langit; keduanya hanya tercatat dalam Edda Prosa yang ditulis Snorri Sturluson pada abad ke-13.
claims.quote: In Norse mythology, Hjúki (Old Norse: [ˈhiu̯ːke] , possibly meaning "the one returning to health") and Bil (O.N.: [ˈbil] , literally "instant") are a brother and sister pair of children who follow the personified Moon, Máni, across the heavens. Both Hjúki and Bil are solely attested in the Prose Edda, written in the 13th century by Snorri Sturluson.

claims.statement: In Gylfaginning chapter 11 High says Hjúki and Bil were fathered by Viðfinnr; once as they walked from the well Byrgir, Máni took them from the earth, and they now follow him in the heavens 'as can be seen from the earth'; Hjúki is otherwise unmentioned.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bab 11 Gylfaginning, High menyatakan Hjúki dan Bil anak Viðfinnr; suatu kali saat mereka berjalan dari sumur Byrgir, Máni mengambil mereka dari bumi, dan kini mereka mengikuti Máni di langit "seperti dapat dilihat dari bumi"; selain itu Hjúki tak disebut lagi.
claims.quote: In chapter 11 of the Prose Edda book Gylfaginning, the enthroned figure of High states that two children by the names of Hjúki and Bil were fathered by Viðfinnr. Once while the two were walking from the well Byrgir ... Máni took them from the Earth, and they now follow Máni in the heavens, "as can be seen from the earth". Hjúki is otherwise unmentioned

claims.statement: Since they are unattested outside the Prose Edda, some suggest Hjúki and Bil were minor figures or Snorri's invention, while Anne Holtsmark (1945) posits Snorri knew a now-lost verse source in which they personified the waxing and waning moon.
claims.statement_id: Karena tak tercatat di luar Edda Prosa, ada dugaan Hjúki dan Bil tokoh mitis kecil atau rekaan Snorri, sedangkan Anne Holtsmark (1945) menduga Snorri mengenal sumber puisi yang kini hilang tempat keduanya mempersonifikasikan bulan yang membesar dan mengecil.
claims.quote: As the two are otherwise unattested outside Snorri's Prose Edda, suggestions have been made that Hjúki and Bil may have been of minor mythic significance, or that they were made up outright by Snorri, while Anne Holtsmark (1945) posits that Snorri may have known or had access to a now lost verse source wherein Hjúki and Bil personified the waxing and waning moon.

claims.statement: Hiuki in Norse mythology was the son of Wildfinnr and brother of Bil; he and his sister were sent to draw water at the well Byrgir and were then taken by Mani, the giant of the moon.
claims.statement_id: Hiuki dalam mitologi Nordik adalah putra Wildfinnr dan saudara Bil; ia dan saudarinya disuruh mengambil air ke sumur Byrgir, lalu diambil oleh Mani, raksasa bulan.
claims.quote: Hiuki war in der nordischen Mythologie der Sohn des Wildfinnr und der Bruder der Bil. Er und seine Schwester wurden zum Brunnen Byrgir geschickt, um Wasser zu schöpfen, woraufhin sie von Mani, dem Riesen des Mondes, zu sich geholt wurden.

claims.statement: They carried on their shoulders the pole Simul (possibly 'eternal') holding the pail Sæg between them.
claims.statement_id: Keduanya memikul di bahu kayu pikulan Simul (mungkin berarti "abadi") yang menggantung ember Sæg di antara mereka.
claims.quote: carrying on their shoulders the pole Simul (Old Norse, possibly meaning "eternal") that held the pail Sæg between them

claims.statement: Scholars have theorised that Hjúki and Bil may represent lunar activity.
claims.statement_id: Para sarjana berteori bahwa Hjúki dan Bil mungkin melambangkan kegiatan bulan.
claims.quote: Scholars have theorized that Hjúki and Bil may represent lunar activity

claims.statement: Hödekin (also Hödeken, Hütgin, Hüdekin and Hütchen) is a kobold (house spirit) of German folklore; the name, a diminutive meaning 'Little Hat', refers to the pileus cap he wears.
claims.statement_id: Hödekin (juga Hödeken, Hütgin, Hüdekin, dan Hütchen) adalah kobold (roh rumah) dalam cerita rakyat Jerman; namanya bentuk kecil yang berarti "Topi Kecil", merujuk topi pileus yang dikenakannya.
claims.quote: Hödekin (variously spelled Hödeken, Hütgin, Hüdekin , and Hütchen , etc.) is a kobold (house spirit) of German folklore. The name, a diminutive meaning "Little Hat", refers to the pileus hat he wears

claims.statement: Hödekin is known for haunting the castle of Bishop Bernard (Bernhardus) of the Prince-Bishopric of Hildesheim in Lower Saxony; in some versions he inhabits Winzenburg, a county he helped the bishopric obtain.
claims.statement_id: Hödekin dikenal menghantui kastel Uskup Bernhard (Bernhardus) dari Keuskupan-Pangeran Hildesheim di Niedersachsen; dalam sebagian versi ia menghuni Winzenburg, wilayah yang dibantunya diperoleh keuskupan.
claims.quote: Hödekin is known for haunting the castle of Bishop Bernard (Bernhardus), Prince-Bishopric of Hildesheim, located in Lower Saxony. In some versions of the legend, the spirit inhabits Winzenburg, a county which he helped the bishopric obtain.

claims.statement: Though he did not start harm, Hödekin was murderously vindictive: he dismembered a kitchen boy who kept insulting him and pouring filth on him, tainted the bishop's meat with toad blood and venom when the cook griped, then pushed the cook into a ditch from a great height, killing him.
claims.statement_id: Meski tidak memulai kejahatan, Hödekin pendendam yang mematikan: ia memotong-motong bocah dapur yang terus menghina dan menuangkan kotoran kepadanya, meracuni daging uskup dengan darah dan bisa kodok saat juru masak mengeluh, lalu mendorong juru masak ke parit dari ketinggian hingga tewas.
claims.quote: Though Hödekin did not initiate harm, he was murderously vindictive. He dismembered a kitchen boy after the boy habitually insulted him and poured kitchen filth upon him. When the cook ... griped, the sprite tainted the meat for the bishop with toad blood and venom. When the cook remained unfazed, Hödekin pushed him into a ditch from a great height, killing him.

claims.statement: Hödeken is the castle spirit of Winzenburg, a dwarf-like figure (kobold) who also carried messages between Hildesheim and Winzenburg; the road between Winzenburg and Hildesheim's Domhof that he reputedly ran to report the last count of Winzenburg's death is called the 'Rennstieg'.
claims.statement_id: Hödeken adalah roh kastel Winzenburg, sosok mirip kurcaci (kobold) yang juga menjadi pembawa pesan antara Hildesheim dan Winzenburg; jalan antara Winzenburg dan Domhof Hildesheim yang konon dilaluinya untuk mengabarkan kematian Graf Winzenburg terakhir disebut "Rennstieg".
claims.quote: Der Hödeken ist der Burggeist der Winzenburg. Er wird als eine zwergenartige Gestalt beschrieben (Kobold), die auch als Bote zwischen Hildesheim und Winzenburg Nachrichten übermittelte. Der Weg zwischen Winzenburg und Hildesheimer Domhof, den Hödeken nach dem Tod des letzten Grafen von Winzenburg entlanggeeilt sein soll, um die Todesnachricht zu überbringen, wird „Rennstieg“ genannt.

claims.statement: Per the Brothers Grimm, Hödeken was a spirit at the court of the Bishop of Hildesheim who kept the night watch awake, gave the bishop military advice, warned him of dangers, sometimes helped other townsfolk, and was once asked to guard a man's wife in his absence.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Grimm bersaudara, Hödeken adalah roh di istana Uskup Hildesheim yang mencegah penjaga malam tertidur, memberi uskup nasihat perang, memperingatkannya akan bahaya, kadang menolong warga Hildesheim lain, dan pernah diminta menjaga istri seseorang selama suaminya pergi.
claims.quote: Der Hödeken war ein Geist, der sich am Hof des Bischofs von Hildesheim aufhielt. Er hinderte die Nachtwachen am Einschlafen, gab dem Bischof militärische Ratschläge und warnte ihn vor kommenden Gefahren. Gelegentlich half er auch anderen Hildesheimern. Einmal bat jemand den Hödeken, seine Frau während seiner Abwesenheit zu beschützen.

claims.statement: He also helped a foolish clerk appointed to the synod with a ring of laurel leaves granting knowledge and intelligence; his time in Hildesheim ended when the bishop exorcised him with ecclesiastical incantations and drove him out.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga menolong seorang juru tulis bodoh yang diangkat ke sinode dengan memberinya cincin daun salam yang memberi pengetahuan dan kecerdasan; akhirnya masa tinggalnya di Hildesheim berakhir ketika uskup mengusirnya dengan mantra gerejawi.
claims.quote: He also helped an idiot clerk appointed to the synod by giving him a ring made of laurel leaves that granted him knowledge and intelligence. Ultimately, the spirit's time in Hildesheim ended when the bishop exorcised him with ecclesiastical incantations and drove him out of the city.

claims.statement: When the man returned, Hödeken complained he would rather herd all the pigs of Saxony than guard such a woman again.
claims.statement_id: Ketika lelaki itu kembali, Hödeken mengeluh bahwa ia lebih suka menggembala semua babi di Sachsen daripada menjaga perempuan seperti itu lagi.
claims.quote: Als der Mann zurückkehrte, beschwerte sich der Hödeken: Er werde lieber alle Schweine von Sachsen hüten als nochmals eine solche Frau.

claims.statement: Per the Grimms, he wore a little felt hat, whence the name Hütchen, in Low Saxon Hödeken.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Grimm bersaudara, ia memakai topi laken kecil di kepalanya, sehingga diberi nama Hütchen, dalam bahasa Saxon Rendah Hödeken.
claims.quote: „[…] auf dem Haupt trug er einen kleinen Filzhut, wovon man ihm den Namen Hütchen auf Niedersächsisch Hödeken gegeben hatte.“

claims.statement: Lyngbakr (Icelandic lyngi 'heather' + bak 'back') is a massive whale-like sea monster said in the Örvar-Odds saga to live in the Greenland Sea; it baited seafarers by posing as a heather-covered island, then sank when a crew landed on its back, drowning them.
claims.statement_id: Lyngbakr (Islandia: lyngi, "heather", + bak, "punggung") adalah monster laut raksasa mirip paus yang menurut Örvar-Odds saga hidup di Laut Greenland; ia memancing pelaut dengan menyamar sebagai pulau berlapis heather, dan bila awak mendarat di punggungnya, ia tenggelam dan menenggelamkan mereka.
claims.quote: Lyngbakr (Icelandic, lyngi "heather" + bak "back") is the name of a massive whale-like sea monster reported in the Örvar-Odds saga to have existed in the Greenland Sea. According to the saga, Lyngbakr would bait seafarers by posing as a heather-covered island, and when a crew landed on his back, he sank into the sea, drowning the crew.

claims.statement: Vignir explained to Oddr that had they landed sooner the crew would surely have drowned; the 'rocks' and 'island' must have been two sea monsters, Lyngbakr, the greatest whale in the world, and hafgufa.
claims.statement_id: Vignir menjelaskan kepada Oddr bahwa bila mereka mendarat lebih cepat, awak pasti tenggelam; "batu" dan "pulau" itu tentulah dua monster laut, Lyngbakr, paus terbesar di dunia, dan hafgufa.
claims.quote: Vignir explained to Oddr that, had they landed sooner, the crew would have surely drowned. The "rocks" and "island" must have been two sea monsters—Lyngbakr, the greatest whale in the world, and hafgufa

claims.statement: The lyngbakur was held the largest of all sea creatures, often lying half-submerged so it seemed an island grown with heather, hence its name; many tales of it are told across Iceland.
claims.statement_id: Lyngbakur dianggap hewan laut terbesar dan sering terapung setengah tenggelam sehingga tampak seperti pulau yang ditumbuhi heather, karena itu disebut lyngbakur; banyak kisah tentangnya tersebar di Islandia.
claims.quote: Lyngbakurinn var talinn vera stærstur allra dýra í sjó og lá hann oft þannig á hálfu kafi að hann virtist vera eyja og leit þá út eins og þar á sé vaxið lyng og því er hann kallaður lyngbakur. Fjölmargar sögur eru um lyngbaka víða frá á Íslandi.

claims.statement: Curious, Oddr decided to turn back and send five men to check the island, but as they approached they saw it and the two rocks had vanished.
claims.statement_id: Karena penasaran, Oddr memutuskan berbalik dan mengirim lima orang memeriksa pulau itu, tetapi saat mendekat mereka melihat pulau dan kedua batu telah lenyap.
claims.quote: Curious, Oddr made up his mind to turn back and send five men to check out the island, but as they approached where the island had been before, they saw that it and the two rocks vanished.

claims.statement: In the saga passage, Oddr sent five men ashore to look for water; soon after they reached the island it sank and they all drowned.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan saga, Oddr menyuruh lima orang naik ke darat mencari air; tak lama setelah mereka tiba di pulau itu, pulau itu tenggelam dan mereka semua mati tenggelam.
claims.quote: Oddr bað fimm menn ganga á land ok leita at vatni. ... En er menn Odds kómu á eyna, höfðu þeir litla stund þar verit, áðr eyin sökk, ok drukknuðu þeir allir.

claims.statement: Inuit folklore of Greenland tells of a similar monster called Imap Umassoursa, and a similar creature appears in the tales of Brendan the Navigator as Jasconius.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inuit Greenland disebut monster serupa bernama Imap Umassoursa, dan makhluk serupa muncul dalam kisah Brendan sang pelaut dengan nama Jasconius.
claims.quote: Í þjóðsögum inúíta á Grænlandi var er talað um svipað skrímsli sem hét Imap Umassoursa. ... Svipuð skepna kemur fyrir í sögunum um Brendan sæfara, sem þar er nefnt Jasconius.

claims.statement: Gewar said that the sacred strength of Balder's body was proof even against steel, but he knew of a sword that could kill him, tightly bound and kept by Miming, the Satyr of the woods, who also had a bracelet of secret virtue that increased its owner's wealth.
claims.statement_id: Gewar berkata bahwa kekuatan suci tubuh Balder kebal bahkan terhadap baja, tetapi ia tahu sebuah pedang yang dapat membunuhnya, terikat sangat ketat dan disimpan oleh Miming, Satir hutan, yang juga memiliki gelang berkhasiat rahasia yang menambah kekayaan pemiliknya.
claims.quote: For he said that the sacred strength of Balder's body was proof even against steel; adding, however, that he knew of a sword which could deal him his death, which was fastened up in the closest bonds; this was in the keeping of Miming, the Satyr of the woods, who also had a bracelet of a secret and marvellous virtue, that used to increase the wealth of the owner.

claims.statement: According to the Italian article, Miming in Norse mythology was a forest-dwelling troll, son of Hothbrod and pupil of Gevar; in a Teutonic version of Baldr's death myth, Miming's sword is the weapon Höðr uses to kill Baldr.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Italia, dalam mitologi Nordik Miming adalah troll penghuni hutan, putra Hothbrod dan murid Gevar; dalam satu versi Teutonik mitos kematian Baldr, pedang Miming adalah senjata yang dipakai Höðr untuk membunuh Baldr.
claims.quote: Nella mitologia norrena, Miming era un troll che abitava nella foresta, era il figlio di Hothbrod e l'allievo di Gevar. In una versione teutonica del mito della morte di Baldr, la spada di Miming è l'arma che Höðr usa per uccidere Baldr.

claims.statement: The tilberi or snakkur is an Icelandic folklore creature made by witches to steal milk; only women can make and own one.
claims.statement_id: Tilberi atau snakkur adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Islandia yang dibuat penyihir untuk mencuri susu; hanya perempuan yang bisa membuat dan memilikinya.
claims.quote: The tilberi (carrier) or snakkur (spindle) is a creature of Icelandic folklore, created by witches to steal milk. Only women can create and own them.

claims.statement: No written record exists before the 17th century, though a 17th-century writer mentions a witch punished in 1500 for owning one.
claims.statement_id: Tidak ada catatan tertulis sebelum abad ke-17, meski seorang penulis abad ke-17 menyebut penyihir yang dihukum karena memilikinya pada 1500.
claims.quote: There are no written mentions of the creatures before the 17th century, although one 17th-century writer mentions a witch being punished for having one in 1500.

claims.statement: The woman steals a rib from a newly buried corpse early on Whitsunday, winds stolen grey wool round it and keeps it between her breasts.
claims.statement_id: Perempuan itu mencuri tulang rusuk jenazah yang baru dikubur pada dini hari Minggu Pentakosta, melilitnya dengan wol kelabu curian, dan menyimpannya di antara payudaranya.
claims.quote: To create a tilberi, the woman steals a rib from a recently buried body early on Whitsunday, twists around it grey wool which she must steal for the purpose and keeps it between her breasts. ...  The next three Sundays at communion she spits the sanctified wine on the bundle, which will come more alive each time.

claims.statement: It returns to the dairy window, calls 'Full belly, Mummy!' and vomits the stolen milk into the churn; to suck an udder it leaps onto the animal's back and stretches itself down.
claims.statement_id: Tilberi kembali ke jendela ruang susu, berseru "Perut penuh, Ibu!", dan memuntahkan susu curian ke pengocok mentega; untuk menyedot ambing ia melompat ke punggung hewan dan memanjangkan diri.
claims.quote: It will return to the window of her dairy and call out "Full belly, Mummy!" or "Churn lid off, Mummy!" and vomit the stolen milk into her butter churn. To suck the milk from the animal's udder, it jumps on her back and lengthens itself to reach down

claims.statement: Butter from milk a tilberi stole clumps or melts into foam if a cross is made over it or the smjörhnútur magic sign drawn in it.
claims.statement_id: Mentega dari susu curian tilberi menggumpal atau mencair menjadi buih bila dibuat tanda salib di atasnya atau digambar tanda sihir smjörhnútur.
claims.quote: Butter churned from milk stolen by a tilberi will clump together as if curdled, or even melt away into foam, if the sign of the cross is made over it or the smjörhnútur (butterknot) magical sign drawn in it.

claims.statement: The tilberi either works itself to death or dies because, as an evil being, it cannot bear the number three; only the human bone remains in the pasture.
claims.statement_id: Tilberi akan bekerja sampai mati atau mati karena, sebagai makhluk jahat, tak tahan angka tiga; hanya tulang manusia yang tertinggal di padang.
claims.quote: The tilberi will then either work itself to death or die because as an evil creature it cannot tolerate the number three. Only the human bone will be left lying in the pasture.

claims.statement: The French article calls the tilberi or snakkur a thief of nearby livestock's milk that turns the butter made from it into gold coins.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Prancis menyebut tilberi atau snakkur pencuri susu ternak sekitar yang mengubah mentega dari susu itu menjadi kepingan emas.
claims.quote: Un tilberi, ou Snakkur est une étrange créature du folklore de l'Islande. C'est une sorte de créature qui vole le lait du bétail des alentours et transforme le beurre fait à partir de ce lait en pièces d'or.

claims.statement: When it arrived it warned the housewife with the words 'Fullur beli, mamma' ('Full belly, Mummy').
claims.statement_id: Saat tiba, tilberi memberi tahu nyonya rumah dengan kata-kata "Fullur beli, mamma" ("Perut penuh, Ibu").
claims.quote: Þegar hann kom, aðvaraði hann húsfreyju með þessum orðum: „Fullur beli, mamma“.

claims.statement: In the belief of the Siberian Yakuts (Jakuten), Ulu Toyon is a demon king ruling the Abaasy, demons of the underworld; he lives in the third heaven and once gave people the secret of fire.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan orang Yakut (Jakuten) Siberia, Ulu Toyon adalah raja iblis yang memerintah Abaasy, iblis dunia bawah; ia tinggal di langit ketiga dan pernah memberi manusia rahasia api.
claims.quote: Ulu Toyon (auch Ulu Toyo'n) ist im Glauben der sibirischen Jakuten ein Dämonenkönig. Er herrscht über die Abaasy, die Dämonen der Unterwelt. Demnach lebt Ulu Toyon im dritten Himmel und gab einst den Menschen das Geheimnis des Feuers.

claims.statement: Ulu Toyon (Yakut: Uluu Toyon, Turkic for 'great lord') is the anthropomorphic head of the evil spirits (abasy), dweller of the upper world and patron of shamans in Yakut mythology.
claims.statement_id: Ulu Toyon (Yakut: Uluu Toyon, dari bahasa Turk "tuan agung") adalah kepala antropomorfis roh jahat (abasy), penghuni dunia atas, dan pelindung dukun dalam mitologi Yakut.
claims.quote: Улу Тойон (якут. Улуу Тойон; от тюрк.  — «великий господин») — антропоморфный глава злых духов (абасы), обитатель верхнего мира, покровитель шаманов в мифологии якутов.

claims.statement: Ulu Toyon is the father of ravens and often appears as one, hence his title 'greatest great raven lord' (Yakut: Uluutuyar Uluu Suorun Toyon).
claims.statement_id: Ulu Toyon adalah ayah para gagak dan sering muncul sebagai gagak, sehingga disebut "tuan gagak agung terbesar" (Yakut: Uluutuyar Uluu Suorun Toyon).
claims.quote: Улу Тойон является отцом воронов, при этом сам нередко предстаёт в обличье ворона, в связи чем его называют величайший великий ворон господин (якут. Улуутуйар Улуу Суорун Тойон).

claims.statement: As patron of shamans, Ulu Toyon judges fairly, settling disputes and punishing those who wronged a shaman.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai pelindung dukun, Ulu Toyon mengadili dengan adil, menyelesaikan perselisihan, dan menghukum orang yang menyakiti seorang dukun.
claims.quote: Являясь покровителем шаманов, Улу Тойон вершит справедливый суд, разрешая споры и наказывая обидевших того или иного шамана людей.

claims.statement: Ergis holds that because of his good traits (granting souls and fire, fair judgement) Ulu Toyon should be counted among the Aiyy; Kulakovsky sees him as abasy in present-day mythology.
claims.statement_id: Ergis berpendapat bahwa karena sifat-sifat baiknya (memberi jiwa, api, pengadilan adil), Ulu Toyon semestinya digolongkan ke roh baik Aiyy; Kulakovsky menilai dalam mitologi kini ia termasuk abasy.
claims.quote: Эргис Г. У. полагает, что из-за проявления добрых черт (наделение душой людей, передача огня, справедливый суд, шаманы-лекари) Улу Тойона следует причислять к числу Айыы.

claims.statement: Ulu Toyon's wife was Buus Dyalkyn Khotun ('icy lady with a waddling gait'); his children were held to be the heads of nine tribes of spirits living in the southern sky.
claims.statement_id: Istri Ulu Toyon adalah Buus Dyalkyn Khotun ("nyonya es dengan langkah terhuyung"); anak-anaknya dianggap pemimpin sembilan suku roh yang tinggal di langit selatan.
claims.quote: Дружиною Улу Тойона була Буус Дьалкин Хотун («крижана пані з розвилистою ходою»). Діти його вважалися главами дев'яти племен духів, що живуть на південному небі.

claims.statement: His true form was believed hidden from mortal sight, but in some myths he appears as a great black bull or black stallion, a huge bear or an elk, running over the earth with a roar.
claims.statement_id: Wujud sejatinya diyakini tak bisa dilihat manusia fana, tetapi dalam beberapa mitos ia tampil sebagai banteng hitam besar, kuda jantan hitam, beruang raksasa, atau rusa besar yang berlari menderu di bumi.
claims.quote: Вважалося, що його справжній вигляд недоступний спогляданню смертних, але в деяких міфах його бачать в образі якогось великої тварини. Так, прийнявши образ великого чорного бика або чорного жеребця, величезного ведмедя чи лося, він з ревом і шумом пробігає по землі.

claims.statement: The Alrune is a legendary being supposedly kept by the ancient Germanic peoples (Germains): mandrakes holding human destiny; in German, Alraune means mandrake.
claims.statement_id: Alrune adalah makhluk legenda yang konon dimiliki bangsa Jermanik (Germains) kuno: mandragora yang menggenggam nasib manusia; dalam bahasa Jerman Alraune berarti mandragora.
claims.quote: L'Alrune est une créature légendaire qu'auraient possédé les anciens Germains. Ce seraient des mandragores qui tiennent le destin des hommes en leur pouvoir (en allemand, Alraune signifie mandragore).

claims.statement: Owners of an Alrune had to dress it, lay it in a little box, wash it weekly with wine and water and feed it at each meal; otherwise, instead of predicting the future, it cried like a starving child.
claims.statement_id: Pemilik Alrune harus mendandaninya, membaringkannya dalam peti kecil, memandikannya tiap pekan dengan anggur dan air, serta memberinya makan-minum tiap bersantap; jika tidak, alih-alih meramal ia menjerit seperti anak kelaparan.
claims.quote: ceux qui possédaient une Alrune devaient l'habiller proprement, la coucher avec attention dans un petit coffret, la laver chaque semaine avec du vin et de l'eau, et lui donner à boire et à manger à chaque repas, sinon, au lieu d'annoncer l'avenir (plus ou moins intelligiblement), elle criait comme un enfant affamé.

claims.statement: The Alraune story dates to the German Middle Ages; alchemists credited the vaguely humanoid mandrake root (Mandragora officinarum) to the semen of hanged men falling on the earth.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Alraune berakar pada Abad Pertengahan Jerman; para alkemis percaya akar mandragora (Mandragora officinarum) yang samar berwujud manusia tumbuh dari sperma orang yang digantung.
claims.quote: A base para a história de Alraune data da Idade Média alemã. A raiz da mandrágora (Mandragora officinarum), que possui um formato vagamente humanóide, era creditada pelos alquimistas como sendo produzida pela ação sobre a terra do esperma de enforcados

claims.statement: Other sources make the Alrune a succubus demon from which the Huns descended, able to take any form but not to change sex.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sumber lain, Alrune adalah iblis sukubus asal-usul bangsa Hun (Huns), yang bisa mengambil segala rupa tetapi tidak bisa berganti kelamin.
claims.quote: Selon d'autres sources, l'Alrune serait un démon succube d'où serait issue la nation des Huns ; elles prendraient toutes sortes de formes, mais ne pourraient pas changer de sexe.

claims.statement: The Alraune is a mandrake root credited with magical properties.
claims.statement_id: Alraune adalah akar mandragora yang dianggap memiliki kekuatan magis.
claims.quote: Альрауна (з нім. Alraune) — корінь мандрагори, якому приписувались магічні властивості.

claims.statement: Magic was ascribed only to roots shaped like a human body; mandrake was mostly sought under the gallows, where a hanged man's remains were supposed to nourish it.
claims.statement_id: Kekuatan magis hanya diberikan pada akar berwujud tubuh manusia; mandragora paling sering dicari di bawah tiang gantungan, tempat jasad orang yang digantung diyakini menyuburkannya.
claims.quote: Магічні властивості приписувались винятково кореням, що мали форму людського тіла. Найчастіше мандрагору шукали під шибеницею, де рештки тіла повішеного повинні були забезпечувати рослині відповідне живлення.

claims.statement: A black dog with a cord from its neck to the plant had to pull the mandrake out; the uprooted mandrake was believed to cry with a human voice that killed the listener, so the dog died.
claims.statement_id: Mandragora harus dicabut oleh anjing hitam yang lehernya diikat tali ke tanaman; mandragora yang tercabut diyakini menjerit dengan suara manusia yang membunuh pendengarnya, sehingga anjing itulah yang mati.
claims.quote: Витягнути мандрагору з землі повинен був чорний пес, якому прив'язували до шиї шнурок, який іншим кінцем був прив'язаний до рослини. Вважалося, що мандрагора, вирвана з землі, кричала людським голосом, який вбивав того, хто її чув; таким чином помирав пес.

claims.statement: To be sure, three magic circles also had to be drawn round the plant with a sword.
claims.statement_id: Untuk berjaga-jaga, tiga lingkaran sihir juga harus digambar dengan pedang di sekeliling tanaman itu.
claims.quote: Для певності треба було ще накреслити мечем три магічні кола навколо рослини.

claims.statement: German writer Hanns Heinz Ewers published a novel titled Alraune in 1911.
claims.statement_id: Penulis Jerman Hanns Heinz Ewers menerbitkan novel berjudul Alraune pada 1911.
claims.quote: O escritor alemão Hanns Heinz Ewers publicou um romance intitulado Alraune em 1911.

claims.statement: In the folk belief of Gotland (Sweden), Bysen is a small forest being who lures people astray or causes trouble for forest workers.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Gotland (Swedia), Bysen adalah makhluk hutan kecil yang memikat orang tersesat atau menyusahkan pekerja hutan.
claims.quote: Bysen är i gotländsk folktro ett litet skogsväsen som lockar människor att gå vilse eller ställer till förtret för skogsarbetarna.

claims.statement: Bysen also delays transports and tips over timber loads; he often appears as a stump or a small, insignificant grey old man and is blamed for all sorts of mischief.
claims.statement_id: Bysen menunda pengangkutan dan menjungkirkan muatan kayu; ia sering muncul sebagai tunggul atau lelaki tua kelabu kecil yang tak mencolok, dan dituduh atas segala kenakalan.
claims.quote: Bysen försenar också transporter och välter timmerlass. Han uppträder ofta som stubbe eller en liten grå, oansenlig gubbe, och beskylls för allt möjligt ofog.

claims.statement: He sometimes wears a red knitted cap and an axe since he must fell Gotland's forest, slowly, at times one tree a century; he is condemned to roam the Earth forever for a crime in life, and also guards forest and nature.
claims.statement_id: Kadang ia bertopi rajut merah dan membawa kapak karena tugasnya menebang hutan Gotland, yang berjalan lambat, kadang satu pohon per abad; ia dihukum mengembara di Bumi (Earth) selamanya atas kejahatan semasa hidup, dan juga penjaga hutan dan alam.
claims.quote: Sometimes he wears a red woven cap and an axe because one of his tasks is to cut down Gotland's forest. This goes slowly, however, and sometimes only one tree per century is felled. It's said Bysen is a humanoid who has done some crime within his lifetime and is therefore sentenced to wander the Earth forever. Bysen is also the ward of the forest and nature.

claims.statement: According to some sources, bysar are dead people who tricked others out of land by moving the markers between two holdings; as punishment they get no rest in the grave.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian sumber, bysar adalah orang mati yang merebut tanah orang lain dengan memindahkan patok batas antara dua bidang tanah; sebagai hukuman mereka tak tenang di kubur.
claims.quote: Bysar är avlidna människor, enligt somliga källor, som lurat till sig någon annans mark genom att flytta de råmärken som markerade gränsen mellan två ägor. Som straff får de ingen ro i graven

claims.statement: If someone follows Bysen and moves the wrong markers back, Bysen finds peace; on the Swedish (svenska) mainland the counterpart is called skälvrängare or osaliga lantmätare, and they mutter 'Här är rätt, här är orätt'.
claims.statement_id: Bila seseorang mengikuti Bysen dan mengembalikan patok yang salah ke tempatnya, Bysen mendapat damai; di daratan Swedia (svenska) padanannya disebut skälvrängare atau osaliga lantmätare, sementara mereka bergumam "Här är rätt, här är orätt".
claims.quote: Om en människa går efter Bysen och flyttar tillbaka de orätta gränsmärkena till rätt ställe, då får Bysen frid. På det svenska fastlandet kallas motsvarigheten skälvrängare

claims.statement: Whoever Bysen sees in the forest has their sight twisted so they cannot find home; turning a garment inside out restores normal sight.
claims.statement_id: Siapa pun yang terlihat oleh Bysen di hutan menjadi kacau penglihatannya sehingga tak bisa pulang; ia dapat memulihkannya dengan membalik pakaian.
claims.quote: Den som Bysen får syn på i skogen, får synen förvrängd, så att denne inte kan hitta hem igen. Den som drabbas kan, genom att vända ett plagg ut och in, återfå normal syn.

claims.statement: The word bys most likely derives from Swedish bus, meaning mischief or prank.
claims.statement_id: Kata bys kemungkinan besar berasal dari kata Swedia bus, yang berarti kenakalan atau keisengan.
claims.quote: The word bys most likely comes from the Swedish word bus, which means mischief or prank.

claims.statement: Bysen (Gutnish: Bysn) is a mythological figure of Gotland folk belief.
claims.statement_id: Bysen (dalam dialek Gutnish disebut Bysn) adalah tokoh mitologis dalam kepercayaan rakyat Gotland.
claims.quote: Bysen (på gutamål Bysn) er en mytologisk figur i gotlandsk folketro.

claims.statement: A female byse is called Bjäru; among other things she steals milk from cows.
claims.statement_id: Bysen perempuan disebut Bjäru; antara lain ia mencuri susu dari sapi.
claims.quote: En kvindelig byse kaldes for Bjäru. Hun stjæler blandt andet mælk fra køer.

claims.statement: Di sma undar jordi (Gutnish for 'the small ones underground', Swedish: de små under jorden), or just di sma, are legendary vættir-like beings in the folklore of the island of Gotland, Sweden.
claims.statement_id: Di sma undar jordi (Gutnish untuk "yang kecil di bawah tanah", Swedia: de små under jorden), atau singkatnya di sma, adalah makhluk legenda mirip vættir dalam cerita rakyat pulau Gotland, Swedia.
claims.quote: or simply di sma, are legendary vættir-like creatures found in folklore from the island of Gotland, Sweden.

claims.statement: Di sma reportedly look after farms and their people and animals unless angered; the classic way to anger them is to scald them carelessly when throwing out hot water.
claims.statement_id: Di sma konon merawat pertanian beserta manusia dan hewannya selama tidak dibuat marah; contoh paling klasik membuat mereka marah adalah menyiram mereka dengan air panas yang dibuang ke luar tanpa berpikir.
claims.quote: Di sma are said to take care of farms and the people and animals that live there, as long as one does not anger them. The most classical example of doing so is to mindlessly scald them when disposing hot water outdoors.

claims.statement: Gotland tales say di sma can only be seen through a hole in a sheet of paper.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah Gotland, di sma hanya dapat dilihat melalui lubang di selembar kertas.
claims.quote: According to Gotlandic tales, di sma can only be seen by looking through a hole in a sheet of paper.

claims.statement: Di sma undar jordi (also spelt di sma undar jårdi) are a Gotland variant of the vättar; folk belief makes them living beings dwelling near people and their farms, who must not have water poured on them without warning.
claims.statement_id: Di sma undar jordi (juga dieja di sma undar jårdi) adalah varian Gotland dari vättar; menurut kepercayaan rakyat mereka makhluk hidup yang tinggal dekat manusia dan pertanian mereka, dan tidak boleh disiram air tanpa peringatan.
claims.quote: Di sma undar jordi (även stavat di sma undar jårdi) är en gotländsk variant på vättar. Enligt folktron är de levande väsen som bor i närheten av människorna och deras gårdar. Man bör inte hälla vatten på dem utan förvarning.

claims.statement: They are really a regional form of the broader lore of the 'hidden people' (mainland Swedish: underjordiska, 'subterraneans').
claims.statement_id: Mereka sebenarnya varian daerah dari cerita rakyat yang lebih luas tentang "orang tersembunyi" (Swedia daratan: underjordiska, "penghuni bawah tanah").
claims.quote: It is really the regional variation of the broader folklore of the "hidden people" (mainland Swedish: underjordiska , "subterraneans").

claims.statement: They are responsible for people caring for the soil and the land.
claims.statement_id: Mereka bertanggung jawab memastikan manusia merawat tanah dan lahan.
claims.quote: De ansvarar för att människorna vårdar jorden och marken.

claims.statement: The Swedish rauk'n'roll band Di sma undar jårdi, active in the 1980s, took its name from these beings.
claims.statement_id: Band rauk'n'roll Swedia Di sma undar jårdi yang aktif pada 1980-an dinamai menurut makhluk ini.
claims.quote: The Swedish rauk'n'roll band Di sma undar jårdi , active in the 1980s, was named after these creatures.

claims.statement: Di sma unda jordi (Gutnish for 'the small ones under the earth' or 'the subterraneans') are a Gotland variant of the vætter.
claims.statement_id: Di sma unda jordi (Gutnish untuk "yang kecil di bawah tanah" atau "penghuni bawah tanah") adalah varian Gotland dari vætter.
claims.quote: Di sma unda jordi (gutnisk for: de små under jorden eller de underjordiske) er en gotlandsk variant af vætter.

claims.statement: The Drak (also Fürdrak, Drakel) is a household spirit of German folklore often equated with the Kobold or devil (Teufel); it is also called Drache (dragon) but has little to do with the reptile monster.
claims.statement_id: Drak (juga Fürdrak, Drakel) adalah roh rumah tangga dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang sering disamakan dengan Kobold atau iblis (Teufel); ia juga disebut Drache (naga) tetapi hampir tak berhubungan dengan naga reptil.
claims.quote: is a household spirit from German folklore often identified with the Kobold or the devil (German Teufel), both of which are also used as synonymous terms for Drak. Otherwise it is also known as Drache (dragon) but has nothing much to do with the reptilian monster in general.

claims.statement: It has been argued that drak does not come straight from Latin draco ('dragon') but from the name mandragora.
claims.statement_id: Telah diajukan bahwa kata drak tidak diturunkan langsung dari kata Latin draco ("naga"), melainkan dari nama mandragora.
claims.quote: The etymology of drak, it has been argued, does not descend directly from Latin draco (German: Drachen, Middle High German: trachen ) for "dragon", but rather from the name mandragora

claims.statement: The Drak (also called Fürdrak, Drakel, Alf, Stöpke and Gluswanz) is a flying house spirit; though it looks like a dragon it probably has nothing in common with one.
claims.statement_id: Drak (juga disebut Fürdrak, Drakel, Alf, Stöpke, dan Gluswanz) adalah roh rumah terbang; meski tampak seperti naga, ia agaknya tak ada kaitannya dengan naga.
claims.quote: Der Drak (oder auch Fürdrak, Drakel, Alf, Stöpke und Gluswanz genannt) ist ein fliegender Hausgeist. Obwohl er äußerlich einem Drachen ähnelt, hat er mit diesem wohl nichts gemeinsam.
